Below is my review of Move Or Die as seen on

Score: 8.5
Bottom-Line: A blast.
Positives:
-Fast-paced, intuitive gameplay
-Perfect party game
-Easy to pick up, hard to master
-Healthy online community
-”Free DLC forever” and mod support
Negatives:
-Arguably a few bucks too expensive
-Visually and architecturally repetitive stages
Move or Die is a blast. It’s fast, hard fun at its simplest. A quick run down of movement controls at the title screen and you’re set to enter the 2D arena, party/playlist chaos. An evolution of Those Awesome Guys’ previous Newgrounds entry Concerned Joe, Move or Die is testament to the developers expertise in fast-paced, quick-fix gaming.
The basic premise is in the name. Keep your globby character in motion or he’ll explode. The rest plays out in a shuffle of various game modes, each of which has its own rules and mechanics. Bomb Tag rigs up one player with a bomb he must hand off before its timer’s up. Rock Run launches a guided missile toward a single player which can be guided into other players. Hat Chase places a single hat in the arena which players must wrestle to wear for longest. The rules are quickly but sufficiently summarized at the start of each of the current 14 modes. It’s incredibly intuitive with plenty of mechanical variables, like randomly placed death, jump, invisible, and teleport blocks, to keep you on your toes.
While they all do their job of mixing things up, some game modes are better than others. Race, while a party-game staple, was definitely the weakest game mode, made so by its repetitive layout. The stage is well designed but lacks in excitement once its track’s been committed to memory: you can’t throw players curveballs once they know what to expect. This is made worse by the fact that environments don’t vary in texture or setting; it all takes place in sleek, laboratory-looking environments. While it wouldn’t wouldn’t have affected gameplay, I feel that varying environment skins to include, say, a jungle, desert, or snow level, would’ve added a pinch more flavor to the otherwise solid visuals. Both issues, however, might be a simple fix in the long run considering the developer’s promise of “free DLC forever” in the form of new game modes, maps, mechanics, and characters. In fact, The developer’s Patch Notes History page outlines previous additions and fixes while an Updates History page previews some of the content in the works. Furthermore, Steam Workshop functionality and an included level creator could help foster a creative community that outlives any developer support.
The current online community, partially remnants from the title’s days in Early Access, is strong and match-making quick. While in lobby, each player must add their preferred game modes to the match playlist to be shuffled between rounds. In my experience, no particular game modes seemed more popular than others so the roulette stayed nice and varied. Servers work great and seem rather forgiving of poor internet connections: I had to conduct my review using a weak connection yet never suffered heavy lag spells or felt like I was put at a disadvantage.
You start out with a handful of characters but quickly develop your roster through levelling up. Most characters feature playful designs, like the pug or skellington. (UPDATE: The zombie character does not in fact take two hits to kill as previously stated.) There currently isn’t a character creation mode but the roster is so large and visually amusing that I never missed one.
While I have few qualms overall with Move Or Die, I do feel that the price of entry may be a touch too high though I guess it depends on how you value your play-time. For me, Move Or Die is most satisfying in 15-minute chunks, played during breaks, quickly before bed, etc. $14.99 is simply a little more than I’d prefer to spend for such casual play sessions. That isn’t to say that it’s a casual game; if you prefer long play-sessions to grind and hone your skills, the high skill-ceiling across the various game modes will keep you plenty busy. The one to four-player local capability makes for a perfect pick-up-and-play party game and may be worth the price in itself, featuring support for up to four controllers or two keyboards while completely playable on a single keyboard. The $40.00 4-pack available on Steam could also make for a sweet split, bringing it down to $10.00 per person if you can assemble a dedicated group.
While most game modes aren't as outright violent as Duck Game, they do see goo-guys popping left and right. Competition is more of a focus on screwing the other players til they mess up and die, as opposed to directly killing them. I’d like to note that my issue with the price is only slight; I really feel like Move Or Die is only a few modes and maps away from becoming a must-buy.
Fast, fun, and satisfying; Move Or Die delivers with next to no filler. The emphasis on “fun” and transparency that Those Awesome Guys set at the core of the game’s promotion and PR, including a 24/7 broadcast of matches played exclusively by AI, seems sincere to me and really helped bolster my appreciation for the title. Consider the Daily Challenges, AI VS, Steam Leaderboards, and upcoming content updates and you’ll have plenty of reason to play today, tomorrow, and next year. Move Or Die is a blast.

You're Rhys. You're captured by a strange man. And guess what? Seems that your friend Fiona is also there. You're on Pandora but in a earlier life, you were an employee of Hyperion. How come you got stuck on the planet? Besides, how come Rhys was searching for you... Oh wait, you're Fiona too! You're a master of deceipts, but hey, you need to survive on your home planet too!
In other words, Tales from the Borderlands is telling you the tale of two individuals coming from two different worlds, being forced to work together to survive... and also to find a vault. Because, hey, vault hunting is fun! The gameplay of the game is to make choices, in words or in actions, because everything will have an impact later. You could cause chaos in a couple or mourn a father figure or even choose to kill people or spare their lives. As Fiona, you're mainly the money keeper - thanks to that, you can buy nice stuff. As Rhys, thanks to the ECHO eye, you can scan around, hack into things or even.... well, you're also the guy with the nice talk and with Handsome Jack, a past baddie, in the head, as an AI uploaded itself in your cybernetic when you didn't suspect a thing.
While the main gameplay is making choices, you have also some good Quick Time Events, mainly in the fifth episode, when you assemble a team with characters you met and take control of Gortys to fight the scary alien.
To resume, Tales from the Bordelands is mainly flashbacks as Rhys and Fiona tell the Stranger the story and have some disagreements about some parts.
In episode 1, Rhys and his best friend Vaughn go on Pandora to steal a deal from Vasquez, Rhys's rival that demoted him to janitorial activity. Unfortunately, the key is revealed to be a fake, thanks to Fiona, her "sister" Sasha and their father figure Felix. And the 10 millions dollars are also stolen by a bandit, so, the five of them have no choice but to run after the money...
In episode 2, after finding an old Atlas facility and a map that could lead to a vault, Fiona, Rhys, Sasha and Vaughn are separated. While the guys deals with Vasquez and for Rhys, with an AI of Handsome Jack in his head, the girls are trying to run from goons interested in her (and a mysterious woman too). Anyway, their main goal is Old Haven, where secrets lie.
In episode 3, the gang, after escaping death from Vallory's gang and Vasquez, meet Athena, the mysterious woman, hired by Felix to protect the girls. And while Gortys is activated, they're going into another old Atlas facility to retrieve a piece of her. Gorthys is indeed a key to open a vault....
In episode 4, Vallory captured the gang because of Gortys. However, the last piece is on Helios, in Handsome Jack's office. So, the gang, without Vaughn, head into Hyperion with a great plan.... that isn't working. It's time for betrayal, for visiting Handsome's Jack office and for some finger guns....
In episode 5, Rhys has been tricked by Handsome Jack, making Hyperion on lockdown. While Fiona, Sasha and Gortys head for the hangar bay, Rhys (and maybe Yvette) go for the power core.... But by destroying it, they're making it crash on Pandora. While Rhys deals with Handsome Jack, Fiona discovers that a monster is guarding the vault and that Gortys can't handle it... However, after that, time passed.... Rhys and Fiona are now prisonners of the Stranger... They're still not done with the Vault of the Traveller....
The game relies a lot on satiric humor, as you're in Borderlands's universe. Rhys and Vaughn aren't skilled to survive Pandora apart with their words and that's the comic part. Also, you can choose to worship Handsome Jack or to come to your senses and to hate him. Gortys has a golden heart and is always cheerful, like a kid and it can be disastrous by moments (and without knowing that she's revealing what she shouldn't). Loader Bot seems also to be very logical but he's very loyal. As for Fiona and Sasha, the comic comes from Pandora's life itself.
The graphics are great too, in cell shader (at least, I think it's called like that). I don't know Borderlands's universe but I think it must fit also the franchise. Also, what is great is also the soundtrack and the songs chosen. It's fitting and besides, the opening sequences are always quite a catch for the eye.
As you understand, you don't need to play Borderlands to understand the game itself. I know that I loose many easter eggs because of that - the signification of the objects in Handsome Jack's office, Scooter's filiation, Athena's story as developed in Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel, Brick and Mordecai... (yeah, I have searched through the Borderlands wiki to understand some things) - but seriously, you can easily plunge into the universe thanks to Tales from the Borderlands.
This game is a must-have. Anyone loving Telltale's games will love it. It changes from the dark world of the Wolf Among Us or the hash reality in The Walking Dead. I'm not regretting to have won it and activated it - nope, it wasn't on Steamgifts but on another site. I don't know if there will be a sequel but if Rhys and Fiona come back, I will be among the firsts to be on board!

A once great game now nothing more than a black hole for your wallets bordom.  Maginogi, coming on 9 years live, has seen better days with more activity.  What can be said?  Nexon, the publishing company for the devcat studio based in Souel, South Korea, has watch its hit game run into the ground.
Nexon is no better, letting employees abuse the job by ban hammering anyone they please or creating chaos without due consequence or respect.  Before Danel Kim showed up with KNoxxr, the infamious CFO, VP to PR; Mabinogi held on to the top 5 list in IGNs best free to play, letting player customize thier "Fantasy Life" and giving them room to follow a path of their own choosing without talent trees to follow.  Mabi once held a hybrid subscription, where you could play as much a you want but things like mainstream storylines and talking with your egos, was not premitted unless you paid the 15$ a month.  Rebirths weren't free either.
So whats changed and does it get my seal?
First off lets look at events.
Events have always had something to remember them by in terms of unquieness.  Now every three months there is a fishing event.  Events now do not reward the player justly as it did 2-3 years ago.  Events are also tuned a step above in terms of difficulty.  So no matter what your doing some event that you just can't solo, and if you do; the reward never fits, ever.
RNG.
RNG, or random number generator, is heavly used in Mabinogi, mainly with life skills.  If you ever enchanted something, you know what I mean, if not this is how it works, mabi never has a 100% garuntee unless it involves quest items.  Now normally 100% meant 100%.  From experence, 100% isnt 100%.  At times the RNG feels more broken then working within the bounds it was meant for.  Even Will Saves don't always roll and check.  That being said it doesn't seem like the game likes playing fair.
Content.
Lately Content seems exhusted from being crapped out every 6 months for huge lore updates.  The latest Saga season feels rushed and doesn't even explain anything past the re washed Ruairi hates everyone and no one live a hapy life.  Old content has now been nerfed.  Honestly, I hate how g1-12 have been reduced, even noobs can take Glas on alone and win.  Although I do get bragging rights for about 90% of my toons passing g3 before nerfdom, the nerf given is a bit extreme.  Without a level cap, or an end game result, nerfing kinda felt pointless.
Leveling.
Leveling no longer require grinding.  Before g17, players were capped at 100, requiring more exp to be gained between times.  Level 30 for most was the start of grindy.  Now players can level to 100 with no problem.  With Mobs that carry the Ancient title, exp is increased greatly for those not label weak against you.
Combat, Loot and game Mechanics.
Ok, here I'll start with combat.
Starting off in G2, you could use the skills you obtained from vairous parts of Ulhaid, and make combos or useful ideas to down a somewhat OP mob.  Now the combat engine features a no load, post-use cooldown.  Effectivly making me feel weaker and using my skill with way more cumbersome use.  Before you could use stradegy or have a unquie fighting style, where now is more number crunching to one hit everything.
Loot is for the most part off and on when it comes to getting that one thing.  For one, Ancients used to drop items that normally you would find in Advance dungeons, Theater Missions, Shadow Missions, or quest items like Fireball shockwave thunder or Ice Spear.  They now drop nothing.  Mabinogi also has annoying times where the loot given for very hard mobs dont fit what so ever.  Where trash drops better than average stuff where the boss drops trash.(Yes some do).  And if your looking to farm gold from Mobs, do not bother.  Your better off playing the market.
Game Mechaincs are the only thing that do make sense.  If someone has a shield and is defending, no matter the skill the cannot be knocked back unless being charged.  SOme mobs have certain restrictions when it comes to fighting them.  However limited, mechanics still exist.
Community is dead.
Customer Support is really a bad joke now.  Submit a ticket and get a response in a week, if your graced with good fortune.  Everyone who answer a ticket is cryptic, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like,♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bag, or plain ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and lazy.  They treat you like♥♥♥♥♥♥and still expect you to be ok with it.  GMs are now not allowed to make them selves public due to a bad day in Dunbarton.  PR is not something Nexon is fond of assocating themselves with.  Modders have even moved on, not to the 5 anti cheating systems now in place, but merely because Nexon will ban anyone for any reason no questions or refunds.
Cash shop.
It has its sales, it has good things.  Mainly more for people who have nothing else to blow money on.
Graphics.
The same when it launched.  Mabi uses an anime style of CGI.  But no improvements have been made since.  Same with Sound.
This is a game for those who once played it, I will never recommend a Nexon game, ever.  Mabinogi is more for those who want nostagla.  Otherwise, your in for a night of swearing.

This game was on my wishlist for months, just waiting for a sale so I could try it out. But, as months went by, it never once dipped in price, and during a night of unfathomable boredom, I decided to take the plunge, forked over the $29.99, and started to play one of the most awesome games ever. Naturally I set a timer to 2 hours in case I wanted a refund, but that wasn't the case, as I was hooked in before the first hour ended, and knew after looking over the modding community, that this game is a keeper. That first time I played it, I didn't stop until the sun rose and I realized it was almost 6 in the morning, after playing for 8 hours straight.
If you are like me and are waiting for a sale -- it seems like that won't happen anytime soon, or at least, it never seems to happen, and this review is to encourage you to take the plunge and have a good time. It is absolutely worth the $29.99, you don't need to wait for a sale, it's worth it, and, while it may not click with you immediately, it is met with "overwhelmingly positive" reviews for a reason, and it is a ton of fun. Very interesting concept too, and executed in a way that is easy to learn, difficult to master, and incredibly addicting regardless of the outcome of your pawns.
Most of my colonies die at one point or another. Most of yours will too. It is not a bad thing, it is not a sad thing, and it shouldn't make you mad, and I don't think it will unless you are like insane about "losing". It's just how the story unfolds, though, and it's part of the game and part of the fun. Another reviewer put it perfectly, saying "Colonies are here for a good time, not a long time". However, sometimes they do last, and it's cool progressing everything, getting more people to join, and experimenting with what to do next as you make it further and further in the new world you are trying to make. Currently my longest lasting colony started out as a tribe of 5 people, but has grown and thrived and may defeat the odds against them in surviving in the world as a colony to be reckoned with. Maybe someday they'll even make it off the planet, if I choose to make it so.
Point is, this game is worth its price tag. Give it a go, you may find yourself immersed in one of the coolest games with a wonderful modding community aiming to make each run a different, engaging, and exciting experience.

Update 11/13/17: Below, I tell you a tale of a distant Rimworld.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
They started as a group of three, crashlanding in a small patch of temperate forest surrounded by the green hell commonly referred to as "tropical rainforests". Akemi was a builder, and a fine one at that, first prioritized building shelter for his fellow survivors. Akemi was accompanied by Kirschi, a former child star that grew into a seasoned actor, charming as hell and good looking to boot, as well as Mal, a roboticist that some considered "too smart".
The first few days were rough. Akemi worked hard to maintain their shelter and even started to build more, in order to stockpile their goods safely, and even considered expanding their little domicile. He was an optimist after all, and crashlanding could just mean a new beginning. He even wanted to give their home a name, declaring it "Greenhell's Oasis". Meanwhile, Mal studied further technologies and applied her intellect to research ways to improve life on this new Rimworld. Kirschi took care of keeping their area clean, but grew restless, as he started to experience withdrawals from his psychite addiction.
For Kirschi, each day without a hit of yayo was a challenge, but he wouldn't break just yet. It was then that the budding colony got its first visitors, some people from a nearby colony that were interested in seeing what exactly fell out of the sky. It was then that Kirschi showed what he could do. What he was born to do - charm and entertain. He talked with each of the visitors and silvertongued his way into their hearts, causing them to break allegiance with their colony and join his cause and his people.
One of them was Skye, an enforcer, and while she was swooned by Kirschi's charm, she saw that at his core, he was an addict, and that he needed help. She decided to arrest him and force him into rehab, a decision that ended up being the best thing for Kirschi, but caused a lot of berserk rages and psychotic breaks on the path to sobriety.
Their numbers grew from three, to eight, and the colony began to thrive. However, this angered their previous chief, causing tension between them and the rising faction that crashlanded only days earlier. A move that could easily turn into a grave mistake if they decide to send raiders for a siege.
However, days went by, then weeks, then months. The colony only grew and prospered, becoming wealthier and more established each day. Their numbers continued to grow, from eight, to ten, to fifteen, until one day, there was an outbreak of malaria. Six colonists were infected, Akemi among them, and had to be forced to rest in the hospital. Lorne, a recent addition to the colony, was a nurse and Skye's father, and he did his best to treat the condition. However, when it rains, it pours.
A myserious plague started to ravage the populace. Twelve colonists were swept by the plague, including Kirschi and Akemi, as well as some others that already had malaria, and only two colonists were considered healthy, Lorne the nurse among them, as well as Mal, the roboticist.
Lorne did what he could, using up most of the stockpiled medicinal herbs, only to find that his efforts were spread so thin, trying to treat everyone, that it was an impossible battle that could not be won. He wanted to break, but he persevered long enough to bury his friends and his daughter, Skye, a real survivor that was taken too soon by a plague that Lorne couldn't cure. Lorne is a broken man now, teetering on the edge of insanity, often having mental breakdowns and hiding in his room.
The colony is mostly deserted now, with Mal being the only founder to have survived this long. Still, while the colonists are beside themselves with grief, they continue on. They can find new members, surely, and hope that such a plague doesn't come back. After all, Mal now sees that they must make it off this planet, and has started to research ship building and all of its intricacies. It may be some time before this happens, but Mal must make sure her comrades' deaths are not in vain.
It's become all too clear. They must get off this Rimworld, but... Will they be able to? Or is this the place where they are all doomed to perish?

I love this game a lot, and I prefer you play it. 9.5/10. There's just one thing you have to know:

Proteus
Proteus is a very interesting piece of work. I don’t call it a game because it doesn’t fit into that category in any traditional sense. It’s less of a game and more of an experiment in musical exploration. After giving it a try for a few hours and seeing a bit of what it offers, I feel confident giving it a solid recommendation for those of you who are looking for something a little different. Allow me to explain why, and perhaps snag your interest.
Proteus begins simply; you open your eyes. You find yourself standing waist deep in the ocean, and can just make out an island off in the distance in front of you. Naturally, you will make your way towards it. Upon reaching the island, it becomes clear that there are some key differences between Proteus and other games. For starters, there is no music until you reach the island. Once you arrive and the music starts to play, you are in for a treat. It is all generated procedurally by what is around you. Frogs, toads, birds and even flowers all play their own notes as you move around and interact with each of them. These sounds combine to form very relaxing musical numbers. The soundtrack, as a result, is a fascinating part of the game. It is in part created by you, the player, and thus becomes a form of gameplay by itself. It’s a brilliant idea put into great use by the developers.
So how about the rest of the gameplay then? It’s equally strange. Upon setting foot on the island, you are left entirely to your own devices. At no point do you ever see text, receive an objective, or have a designated goal handed to you. You are entirely on your own. And that’s exactly how it should be. Explore, find hidden little secrets and tidbits and write your own story! When you are prepared to quit, you don’t simply press escape and use a menu to quit. Instead you hold down the escape key, and your eyes begin to close. Quitting is represented as returning to sleep. When you’re ready to play again, you once more open your eyes and find yourself standing waist deep in water, with an entirely new, procedurally generated island waiting for you in the distance. Each new game is a new day, a new world, and a new opportunity for discovery.
I personally came away from Proteus filled with wonder, and far more relaxed than when I went in. It is almost meditative rather than being tense and stressful. For anyone with an open mind looking to try something new, Proteus is a fantastic and beautiful way to relax and pass the time. There’s nothing else quite like it on the market. The most closely related comparison would come from last year’s Playstation 3 exclusive title, Journey, by ThatGameCompany, and that is a glowing comparison to a fantastic game. Proteus is a great little title in a sea of big-budget blockbusters, and should not be overlooked. Give it a shot, you may find yourself pleasantly surprised.

I've made a review before finishing the game, and now I'm going to review again.
This game isn't the best RPG I ever played, but I garantee you, it'll be one of the most funny and enjoyable since Skyrim.
+ Good story, but with some clichés
+ Great improvement in voice acting (still, the main character's is aweful) comparing to the previous games in the series
+Despite the game's engine being old, the shadow and lightning effect is one of the best out there, providing beautiful and colorful scenarios
+ Cool artwork
+ Most of the quests are original and they don't repeat a lot.
+ Tons of secret treasures and chambers to be discovered
+ It give's you that Gothic series feeling, which is really nice
+ Combat system is captivating...
-... if you get through the first hours frustration
- Soundtrack is just decent, it could be much better
- Face expressions are pratically nonexistent
- There could be more to loot in the maps
- The ship battles are cool, but it gets old real quick
- Some missions are just tedious
- Some bugs here and there
- IA is mediocre, companions get lost frequently and after some hours in the game, the enemies are just dead meat
-Dialogues are too lengthy
- If you played Risen 2, you'll recognize most of the scenarios, since they are basically the same
Final: If you can get through the frustration of the first hours, you will discover a magnificent and original RPG, that gives a perfect balance between a pirates and a common RPG theme. There's a discover here, the scenarios are incredibly rich, there's secrets everywhere, and the story is compelling. Of course, you can see that the budget wasn't very high: The combat system suffered great improvements, but it lacks some adjustments; the voice acting could be a lot better; the game engine is recycled (still, huge improvements!), some bugs are just really annoying. But still, this game is a must have in every RPG-lover collection. Specially the Gothic fans. Seriously, it's the first time in a decade that a game gives me a Gothic game feeling.
Final Score: 8/10

I think there's one character that truly captures the game's problems: your sister. I can imagine that design meeting:
"Ok, we need a girl in the game. What do we know about girls? Uh... they have boobs. Good, perfect. Make them huge, because pirates would value the extra buoyancy. Now we have a boob pirate... oh! But let's be different, and instead of eye candy she's your SISTER! Right... so, what do brothers and sisters talk about? Being brother and sister, of course! Make sure that she reminds you with every sentence. That way the player is convinced that she's both a boob pirate AND your sister. It's called immersion. Look it up."
I don't think the game was actually written by a real writer.
I've played it for 12 hours. I will probably beat it, and I actually enjoy the game a little despite itself.
The overall issue that will prevent me from ever truly recommending the game is how poorly-devised the world is. The writing is stupid -- and I use the word "stupid" because it really is the most accurate. It's simply dumb. I actually find myself sympathizing with the writing at times, because the problems remind me so much of the "books" I wrote as a young teen (I'm almost 30). Characters say things ALL THE TIME that create a hundred different questions.
"If he uses magic he'll die like all the others."
What others? Who died? Who used magic and had it go poorly? Why does everyone treat magic like it's a part of life, a boon, or a blessing, and then this character acts like it's certain doom OUT OF NOWHERE. Why does no one else reflect this? Why haven't I been presented with lore? Why didn't you use this opportunity to GIVE me lore.
"If you don't do this you'll die."
How do you know that? Where could this knowledge have possibly come from? Why does the main character not find any of this strange?
Those are just two small examples in what feels like an absolute barrage of inconsistencies. I don't feel like a world has been created here. It feels like a few game designers sat around and threw around cliches at each other until they had a script.
The main character suffers three-fold: for some reason they wanted him to look like an unlikable version of Christian Bale. His voice actor (or the director) can't seem to nail the mood of a single line. You're constantly being reminded through his gruff cursing that this is a recording of an actor in a booth somewhere, and not a real person. And third, his writing is terrible -- both in WHAT he says, and in his robustness as a character.
Some of the voice actors truly are great. There are good performances that stand out, despite the rest of the game. That point needs to be made. But even these GOOD performances have issues. I feel like no one directing the game's talent had any true vision for what the game was supposed to be or how lines were supposed to be delivered. It feels like a discovery-writer's first draft. OR, the opposite problem, they could have had TOO many creative hands in the development. This is an issue of leadership and vision.
Perhaps the absolute worst thing about the game is that when it makes me laugh (and it does, it can be quite funny), I'm not completely certain the game MEANT to make me laugh. I'm fairly certain the "funny parts" are supposed to be when people curse. I just don't believe the creators were capable of intentionally making me belly-laugh. I don't know if I'm laughing with or at this game.
I go back to my earlier comment: this game is stupid, and I hate using that word to describe things. The game labors tirelessly to convince you that not a single talented designer has ever touched Risen 3. I enjoy it a little, and am rather determined to finish it. But every single person who had a creative hand in this game's writing, design and acting needs to take a long, hard look at other themselves or other professions. I would be embarrassed to ask people for money for this game, and I feel foolish having given them the benefit of the doubt.

As of v0.7.3.4:
Subterrain is a top-down survival game set on underground Mars colony.
Something went terribly wrong, everyone's turned into terrible monsters and your only task is to survive.
To make sure you survive, you need food, water, good suit (since it can be freezing or too hot in some parts of the colony), large backpack for your loot and, of course, a gun.
Subterrain is primarily a game about surviving and only after that about everything else (craft, combat, etc).
That's probably why the survival and exploration aspects feel like the most polished ones, while combat and crafting feel pretty basic (although, since the game is in early access, that might as well change until release).
You'll be spending most of your time going around pretty large open world (that is nonetheless is split into areas with loading screens) of the underground colony looking for useful things and monsters to kill. And you'll die a lot in the process.
I found that the best approach for me was to clean out one of the areas and set up a base there - with crafting and research stations, power generator and some lockers for storage.
Having access to power generator is probably one of the most important things in the game - not only does your battery powers your flashlight, but it's also used by your guns.
You do have an option to use a melee weapon, but in my opinion melee combat is just not very good at the moment - you get staggered a lot, there's no way to evade enemies attacks, so it's just turns into a clicking and endurance test.
Using guns are a bit more fun - you get to run away from attackers while shooting back, but that's about it. As I mentioned earlier - combat is not the strongest point of the game.
After gathering enough things you can craft new gear (including modular pistols), research parts of the monsters you was able to gather, synthesise cure and prepare for your next trip.
No major bugs, issues or crashes were encountered during my playtime.
Game does have some small user experience problems (e.g. ESC doesn't closes all menus, no hotkey to pickup all from container - you need to click, no tooltips for items in hotbar) - but they are insignificant and will most likely be fixed (since it's quite easy to do so).
One of the biggest things for me is the fact that there's no manual save game. I do understand that the game wants to be "hardcore", but would prefer an option to save more and try out different things.
If that sounds OK - go for it. There's plenty of content and enough stuff to do for hours.
So, just to sum that up - if you are looking for combat oriented game, better look elsewhere.
But if you want a survival and exploration game that's quite challenging - you're probably gonna have a lot of fun with Subterrain.

There is a variety of classes available, enough to satisfy every squad's needs. Although the basic rifleman is too often shunned for other better-equipped classes. The community is generally friendly, as well as helpful to beginners (and we like it to stay that way). Tred carefully, stay alert, look out for your team, and you'll have a good time.

After playing for a couple of months (not Steam version, because the Steam launcher was giving me troubles)
— June 2014 — due to the overall impression I’ve got. Read the details below and be prepared if you want to buy the game.
I know it is a game but if you don’t prepare properly, you will regret it. Or you will quit the game much earlier. A free trial for 14 days is available to anyone. Any Eve Online player can send you a link for a free trial for 21 days. You can choose to pay the subscription or enter the CD code from a starter pack at any time. Your trial time will not disappear. Your paid time will just be added to the trial time. So always start as a trial. No need to waste 14-21 days.
It is a sandbox game. Unlike theme park games where gamers can interact with what developers have created to have fun, in sandbox games you have to create your own fun. The PvP (player versus player) component of the game clearly outweighs the PvE (player versus environment) component.
Choosing your race or bloodline is not very important. Stats are the same. Only for role players it is important. Caldari area has the largest trade hub in the game at the moment. You start the game as a member of an NPC corporation. You can join a player-run corporation at any time. Learning the game alone is difficult. Join the corporation Eve University or some other corporation that is friendly to new players. Having a mentor to ask stupid questions is very handy.
Very important. A new character is given three character attribute remaps. You can use them to tune five attributes of your character in quite a wide range. Every skill requires a primary attribute and a secondary attribute. The amount of skill points you have in a specific attribute determines the speed of “learning” a particular skill. Benefits of the primary attribute affect the skill learning speed in full while benefits of the secondary skill give half as much speed. A new player gets two bonus remaps and one regular one. Once you spend them, your next remap will be available only one year after! These attributes are important only for learning. Nothing else.
Never train rank V of a skill unless it opens up another skill that you want. Rank V is designed for perfectionists only!
Unlike other games in Eve Online you cannot accelerate your character levelling by putting more personal time and effort into it. You can only install implants that give bonuses to your primary attributes. They vary from +1 to +5 attribute points. These implants speed up levelling. Implants + properly maxed attributes for specific skills are vital. Besides, if you buy any starter pack, you get a cerebral accelerator that gives a massive boost to attributes for a short time like 14 days (+9 to each attribute), 35 days (+3) or 7 days (+17 or 19, I don’t remember). The accelerator works for characters younger than the specified age. The effect will stay with you between the time you inject it and the time you reach that age. After that you cannot inject it.
Unless you are a genius and know the game inside out you must get the program EveMon to plan your character progression. Eve Online is spreadsheets in space and takes a lot of calculations. It is not for impatient people, who want to do everything the game has to offer in a couple of months. A properly skilled character can take a year to get.
One thing is good, however. The game has a skill queuing system. You learn skills while offline as long as your subscription time is paid. The queuing skill clearly outlines when your skills get learned.
Every solar system has a security level. 1.0 is the highest one and 0.0 is the lowest one. The range from 1.0 till 0.5 is called highsec. In highsec space police (aka CONCORD) will interfere if you fire upon or get fired upon without a war declaration. In this space you are kind of safe. The range from 0.4 till 0.1 is lowsec. Police will not interfere although the personal security ranking of the player, who commits a crime, will drop. If it is too low, such players will be hunted down by police upon entering highsec space. 0.0 is the null security space or nullsec where no rules apply but what you make. Don’t go there unless you are prepared.
The back end of the game is much more than what you are used to in any other game. You will see how much ISK (in-game currency) you spent or gained every time. You will be able to see every trade between you and some other character. Lots and lots of text. Lots of text as tutorials at the start of the game. Some people complain that it looks like you accept a lot of license agreements.
UPDATE
Until recently you couldn't fly using WASD. Double-click on empty space and you will fly in that direction. Or choose a marker from the overview (a list of objects that exist around you in outer space, five tabs max, mind-blowingly customizable), right-click and choose Approach or Warp or something. The game has a lot of right-click and choose an option stuff. Practically core gameplay.
The game was released in 2003. It has been updated since but still doesn’t look too good. For instance, with all settings on max and shaders at low it will look its best. Music is okay but I wish it had soundtracks similar to music from The Swapper. Sound effects are nothing to write home about.
The game development looks slow. CCP, the development studio, seems to pool all the human resources together and then use them on various projects when a need arises. CCP has a record of promising features and not delivering them. Coming from other games where every expansion offers a tonne of content, I cannot say that Eve Online expansions offer a lot. Probably because game developers don’t stick with CCP for too long.
CCP also seems to suffer from being too ambitious and from the lack of a clear and integral vision of how their games should develop. Google “CCP world of darkness” or “CCP Incarna” to learn about the game developer’s PR failures.
They are the people you will interact with all the time. They can play the game for different purposes. Beware that scamming in the game is allowed. You cannot open a ticket and get anything restored. Read what you pay for carefully.
The veteran players of Eve Online consider the game a game for elite gamers and the attitude can be felt easily on the forums. In the game the attitude is mostly friendly. However, they expect those, who want to continue playing the game after trial, to put effort and time in learning the game properly.
Go for it if you have a buddy in a corporation that does a lot of PvP. You are likely to participate in fights from day one. You will lose your ships a lot but the corporation is supposed (ask whether your corporation does it) to reimburse newbie ships since they don’t cost much for veteran players unless you lose the ships in particularly stupid ways.
Go for it if you are reading the text much time later and the game has improved by a lot. The things I’ve learned about the new industry UI in Eve Online in summer 2014 is a promise of a better future.

You're Rhys. You're captured by a strange man. And guess what? Seems that your friend Fiona is also there. You're on Pandora but in a earlier life, you were an employee of Hyperion. How come you got stuck on the planet? Besides, how come Rhys was searching for you... Oh wait, you're Fiona too! You're a master of deceipts, but hey, you need to survive on your home planet too!
In other words, Tales from the Borderlands is telling you the tale of two individuals coming from two different worlds, being forced to work together to survive... and also to find a vault. Because, hey, vault hunting is fun! The gameplay of the game is to make choices, in words or in actions, because everything will have an impact later. You could cause chaos in a couple or mourn a father figure or even choose to kill people or spare their lives. As Fiona, you're mainly the money keeper - thanks to that, you can buy nice stuff. As Rhys, thanks to the ECHO eye, you can scan around, hack into things or even.... well, you're also the guy with the nice talk and with Handsome Jack, a past baddie, in the head, as an AI uploaded itself in your cybernetic when you didn't suspect a thing.
While the main gameplay is making choices, you have also some good Quick Time Events, mainly in the fifth episode, when you assemble a team with characters you met and take control of Gortys to fight the scary alien.
To resume, Tales from the Bordelands is mainly flashbacks as Rhys and Fiona tell the Stranger the story and have some disagreements about some parts.
In episode 1, Rhys and his best friend Vaughn go on Pandora to steal a deal from Vasquez, Rhys's rival that demoted him to janitorial activity. Unfortunately, the key is revealed to be a fake, thanks to Fiona, her "sister" Sasha and their father figure Felix. And the 10 millions dollars are also stolen by a bandit, so, the five of them have no choice but to run after the money...
In episode 2, after finding an old Atlas facility and a map that could lead to a vault, Fiona, Rhys, Sasha and Vaughn are separated. While the guys deals with Vasquez and for Rhys, with an AI of Handsome Jack in his head, the girls are trying to run from goons interested in her (and a mysterious woman too). Anyway, their main goal is Old Haven, where secrets lie.
In episode 3, the gang, after escaping death from Vallory's gang and Vasquez, meet Athena, the mysterious woman, hired by Felix to protect the girls. And while Gortys is activated, they're going into another old Atlas facility to retrieve a piece of her. Gorthys is indeed a key to open a vault....
In episode 4, Vallory captured the gang because of Gortys. However, the last piece is on Helios, in Handsome Jack's office. So, the gang, without Vaughn, head into Hyperion with a great plan.... that isn't working. It's time for betrayal, for visiting Handsome's Jack office and for some finger guns....
In episode 5, Rhys has been tricked by Handsome Jack, making Hyperion on lockdown. While Fiona, Sasha and Gortys head for the hangar bay, Rhys (and maybe Yvette) go for the power core.... But by destroying it, they're making it crash on Pandora. While Rhys deals with Handsome Jack, Fiona discovers that a monster is guarding the vault and that Gortys can't handle it... However, after that, time passed.... Rhys and Fiona are now prisonners of the Stranger... They're still not done with the Vault of the Traveller....
The game relies a lot on satiric humor, as you're in Borderlands's universe. Rhys and Vaughn aren't skilled to survive Pandora apart with their words and that's the comic part. Also, you can choose to worship Handsome Jack or to come to your senses and to hate him. Gortys has a golden heart and is always cheerful, like a kid and it can be disastrous by moments (and without knowing that she's revealing what she shouldn't). Loader Bot seems also to be very logical but he's very loyal. As for Fiona and Sasha, the comic comes from Pandora's life itself.
The graphics are great too, in cell shader (at least, I think it's called like that). I don't know Borderlands's universe but I think it must fit also the franchise. Also, what is great is also the soundtrack and the songs chosen. It's fitting and besides, the opening sequences are always quite a catch for the eye.
As you understand, you don't need to play Borderlands to understand the game itself. I know that I loose many easter eggs because of that - the signification of the objects in Handsome Jack's office, Scooter's filiation, Athena's story as developed in Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel, Brick and Mordecai... (yeah, I have searched through the Borderlands wiki to understand some things) - but seriously, you can easily plunge into the universe thanks to Tales from the Borderlands.
This game is a must-have. Anyone loving Telltale's games will love it. It changes from the dark world of the Wolf Among Us or the hash reality in The Walking Dead. I'm not regretting to have won it and activated it - nope, it wasn't on Steamgifts but on another site. I don't know if there will be a sequel but if Rhys and Fiona come back, I will be among the firsts to be on board!

I've been struggiling with the Review of this game for a while, but at the end I've come to the conclusion that I can't recommend ist. Mainly because its hardly a game. But it is not all bad. Just not enough for me to recommend it.
It follows the new Telltale formula very closely, so each of the five episodes is a two hour movie with some quick time events thrown in, which I see as bad excuse for gameplay. Since the game is also available on mobile devices without major changes, all the interactivity centeres around them, so don't expect anything more than simple swipe gestures, which are somewhat weird to do with a mouse. I played with a controller (anything XInput compatible like an XBox360 controller should work, I used a Logitech F310), as I tend to lean back in my chair when watching movies on my computer, but when got surprised with a QTE, I smash my hands against the table trying to get to the keyboard and mouse in time. So having a controller in my lap is more comfortable.
From a technical standpoint the game is not on par with anything released in the last 5+ years on PC: The animations are wooden, the facial expressions and gestures of the characters are worse than in Borderlands 2 (and that is an FPS!) and the overall texturework and detail of the characters and evironments profits from Borderlands' cellshaded look, therefore does not look as bad. I do have to say they mimic the style quite nicely, combined with some superb voice acting and good music it feels like a Borderlands' game, or more like a Borderlands movie. And I like Borderlands, especially the second game, thats why I gave the game a shot despite my resevations against games with the Telltale formula.
The characters are diverse and colorful, as I would expect it from a Borderlands game. But they just don't feel as fleshed out as the ones in the other games (particullary Borderlands 2) and their development seems very rushed, especially with the main character Rhys. He transforms from defualt Hyperion employee to badass in mere minutes, while Fiona always stays the cunning con artist she is. The game focues on the new characters, some from previous games appear but for the most part only play support roles. One of them is Handsome Jack, which they managed to put in the game. It makes for some good dialogue and scenes, but the "how" is not very good. I also think they overused his character to the point where he becomes blant. I really like him in Borderlands 2, he makes for one of the best antagonist in any game because you can understand his motives. You don't have to agree with him, but you can understand why he acts that way and as a clear an wellpaced development over the course of the game, which makes him more ... human.
I experienced the five quite differently: The first one is a good introduciton, you get to know all the new characters and the basic setting. But with the second and third episode a decline in quiality is undeniable, it feels like the story in moving nowhere and the humor is just not there. It also took Telltale quite a while to release the episodes, their are long gaps between the first three episodes and with the cliffhanger at the end of the second one it was just painful.
The fourth episode is by far the best, finally the story gets really going and the humor is almost on par with Borderlands 2. But it also has the worst und most unnecessary scene in the entire game. I don't want to spoil anything, but it centers around the death of a character. Nothing new in the world of Telltale games, but this one feels forced: it is unnecessary, unrealistic und overall just to create some tragedy in the cheapest way possbile. The circumstances are illogical and just plain stupid. It feels like the through: "Oh, we need some tragedy before the big finale, how can we get that?" "We could kill a character, why not this one?". And then they just did, but it makes absolutly no sense and just there to create an emotional reaction, but in the cheapest way possible.
The fith episode is not as good as the fourth one, mainly because the gags are not as good and ofte anymore, it gets more serious towards the ending. That itself is not bad and makes for a good finish of the whole game. Choices from previous episodes do matter (take notes Mass Effect devs!), how much I cannot tell since I would have to play the game again with different choices, but I don't think I can bring myself to do that.

Alright, if you thought Gone Home "wasn't a game" because it didn't involve shooting dudes in the face well you really won't like this one.  Proteus puts you on a procedurally-generated island, with graphics that will show off the horsepower of your new 386.   It's a vacation to a magic land of pixelated trees and wildlife, where fireflies dance in the woods at night and a circle of mysterious stones can take you to the next season - spring, summer, fall and winter all have different characters.  There's an ending of sorts, but the entire game is calm, slow, plotless, but graphically stunning in its low-resolution way. Certain vistas made me gasp or smile when I moved through them. Proteus is digital antidepressant and well worth experiencing from time to time when you need to destress.

A strange take on the zombie apocalypse and to an extent, on strategy games on the whole. From the game's surf soundtrack, to it's hokey comic vignetttes, to the ridiculous randomized names of your squads, to the foghorn of the rescue chopper, everything is a little off kilter. The thing is, this game has a lot going for it in my eyes. The gameplay is absolutely on point. From the macro boardgame map where every mission you do effects the spread of the zombies and how many points you gain towards overall campaign victory, to the micro boards, where every second your snipers can fire and every scientist you can rescue on a mission matters. The game has both a planning phase and an action phase. The planning phase takes place before the mission begins in full, and allows you to place all your units, some which you can move later, and some which you can't. You'll have to be careful though because they CAN be killed, and barriers can be avoided if a gas line ruptures and the following building collapse eliminates your chokepoint. Then, in the action phase, the zombies start flooding in, the chopper flies over, and you can start blowing things up with your artillery. The random city designs force you to think critically and adapt on every single level, and if you're playing with base game rules, the rotation of available squads will also force you to get good at more than one playstyle. I don't want to spoil too much, because I found a lot of the fun came in the surprises of the new challenges presented as the campaign progressed, and the new troops and comics you unlock while playing. I really respect what was done with the base game, but if you don't like it, you can change pretty much any setting you could think of, and if not, there's a simple ingame mod system which can change even more stuff, if you like. Altogether pretty brilliant, and if nothing else, you should really try the demo for a sample and to check that it runs well on your PC. 8.5/10 because of how refreshing and exciting it was.

I used to hate this game's guts. I don't know what it was (this was a few years back) - the cutesy character designs, the clunky combat, or the complete lack of a discernable main quest. However, I've recently given it another try - and damn is it a good game.
Mabinogi is a sandbox MMORPG published (unfortunately) by the (in)famous Nexon - so of course, it's a KMMO. Don't let that turn you away if you're afraid of the grind usually associated with games like MapleStory and Ragnarok though! The game has rather unique mechanics that keep the game from ever really feeling like a slog. The game came out in 2003 (and it hardly looks it), and has been consistently updated with more content.
The game is heavily focused around 'life skills' - generally non-combat skills, such as fishing, tailoring, and even songwriting. That's not to say that you can't crawl through dungeons and slay beasties, however. It merely gives you the opportunity to take a break, play the lute (unfortunately, there's no Lute Hero minigame), mine some ores, or make some clothes. You can even build up a base in what's oddly similar to a Farmville clone in a separate instance from the main world. As you craft, kill, and gather, you'll earn experience both towards your character level and your skill levels. As you increase your skills and advance them with the use of Ability Points (earned from level-ups and quests), you'll also gain permanent stat increases for your character, from HP to Intelligence. These permanent stat gains seem minor at first, but as you start branching out your skills (you go from ranks E to A, then 1 to 9 in each skill), your character will become much more formidable, and you'll unlock stat-altering titles to boot.
The most unique thing about the game is the Rebirth system. After your character's been around for a week real time, you can have them be "reborn" and reset to level 1 (and change their appearance if you so desire). The benefit to this is mostly farming AP, but your skills and permanent stat ups remain. Leveling up, for this reason, doesn't take an obscene amount of time.
Questing in the game is, unfortunately, rather generic. You'll randomly gain "Hunt" quests (kill quests), but you can also talk to NPCs to start quests that have at least some minor amount of plot to them (though they still amount to fetch/kill quests). The flavor text does add life to the game world, as there's usually some reason you're being told to slaughter wolves or crawl through the local hive of spiders. Along with this are the Story quests and the Event quests. Events are usually to mark a large release, such as character animal transformations, or a holiday. Story quests vary from a Mabinogified version of Shakespear's Hamlet (no joke; it's amazing experience, too) to the typical "the goddess sent you to x" RPG fare. Still, I can't help but smile at the quest complete jingle.
Speaking of music, holy Christ in Heaven, this game has a top tier soundtrack. Whether you're adventuring on the open plain, relaxing in town, or slaying beasts in the caverns below, the music is bound to have you grinning or humming along. My personal favorite tune is in Tir Chonal [or however you spell it], the human starting town.
Unfortunately, as far as I can tell in my 15 hours of play (I have more off of Steam), there doesn't seem to be any real endgame beyond the Advanced and Expert dungeon crawls. If someone could correct me on that, I'll put a note in the end of the review.
Overall, I have to recommend you at least try the game if you don't absolutely despise anime (which this game is drenched in the cologne of). It's a fun game, and you have nothing to lose but temporary computer space.

Subterrain is an indie horror survival game that has simplistic controls and a few jump scares. I honestly wasn't expecting a game with these types of graphics to actually scare me but it managed to very well. The whole concept of this game is a nice one, there are many zombie games out there but this one tries to be different by being set entirely underground. My impression of the game changed after the intro, when I actually got a chance to dive into the gameplay I was pleasantly surprised. The graphics and gameplay are similar to that of the SAS Zombie Assault series, but of course this is not a tower defense, it tells a nice story where you must learn what happened and how to escape the enemy. You also have to use a little strategy when playing because you must collect food and conserve ammo and not blow it all on one enemy.
There currently seems to be minimal instruction in the tutorial, I found myself basically thrown into the wild with no real clue what to do in the beginning. Also I find that the rate of which you become thirsty is slightly too advanced and can perhaps be slowed down a bit. Also in the tutorial the beginning enemies you face can be difficult, taking away a lot of my health but not as easy to find and use items to regain your health.
However it is still early access and I would recommend this game to those who enjoy similar games in the same genre.

My current state when writing this report:
70h of offline gametime, no MP gametime.
Story completed.
"side quests" compleded and only trying to get the best rank in all of them atm.
Pros:
- create your own character and fight in DBZs history.
- big selection of cloth to wear and customize your avatar.
- many "side quests" with additional battles to fight (called parallel quests in game).
- a good selection of playable character for multiplayer or as partner in side quests.
- great selection of skills to select from (physical / ki / transformation / evasion)
Cons:
- The main story is not completable unless you lvl up by doing side quests, and i dont mean just do all of them once...
- all pieces of gear you can get have boni and mali on them so changing into the outfit you like most may not give you the boost in stats you focus on.
- and of course the BIGGES ANNOYANCE is RNG.
RNG realy rules this game:
Every sidequest has severa rewards, usually a few skills and one or two armor sets you can get.
At first it sounds nice but once you try getting them you start you will notice the RNG chain.
A side quest has always 1 win and at least 1 loose condition, after that there are 2 additional condition that are hidden.
If you manage to clear the hidden conditions you have the CHANCE for an additional encounter, yes only a CHANCE.
That additional encounter is most of the time which will stopp you from getting the skill, gear and of course Z-Rank you want.
Even if you are lucky enough to get the enemy to spawn and beat him or them the next dice is rolled.
Will you get that piece you want? Nah, probably not.
Those encounters happen rarely (in my case) and if you are lucky to get a drop no one says its not one you already have.
I am sure you can imagine how frustrating it is to try and get a full set of gear (body, pants, gloves and boots)
... let the grind begin.
Fazit:
Even if the game can probably be beaten in a single day if only the necessary levels are played (and grinded) it is still a fun game. Trying to max your char(lvl80), getting the skills together you want and boosting your stats with the right gear to break your opponent with powerfull attacks gives quite the satisfying feeling as long as long as you have the patience to roll the dice a mio. times. Beware of multiplayer since the game can realy easily be manipulated with simple tools like cheat engine.

This game is actually pay2win, pure and simple.
It's one of those games where the whales who pay, like to pretend that it's "pay to grind".

The amount of grind makes sure that any new gadget or item that comes out is exclusive to those who pay for a while. Just try asking around how much grind is needed to get something you can buy for 40$, and it'll give you and idea by how people respond to this.
Besides, when enough people can actually grind those items, they come out with new stuff.

It's not "pay to win those parts are just imbalanced".

It's cute, it's fun for a while, there's lots of explosions, so perfect if you have short attention span and are easily impressed by EXPLOSIONS!!!!

Then at around level 5, pay2win kicks in.
The good thing is that it only takes about 5 hours to get to that level, so you will hopefully not be too invested in the game.

If you do get invested, I expect you to come back and try to deflect from any of those points with anecdoted about that one player who has grinded so much that he made more money than anyone has ever paid, which will completely miss the point, because it won't be the normal experience of most people.

It's like what EA did with Star Wars Battlefront II, but there a bit more obfuscation to it, so, people don't notice right away. EA should look into this game, to see if they employ their patent of matching people who buy with worse players than them, to make them win more. It's completely plausible it's being used in this game.


Having read a bit more about the evolution of the game, here's how it works.
They push new content out, whales buy it day one, and kill everyone with it, literally pay 2 win.
But wait, you can grind!
Yeah, but, by the time most people got them, new content, more powerful content!
At the time of this writing, people are mad at drones, which, "is completely unbalanced, why aren't they fixing it!?!"

They aren't fixing it because enough people are buying it because it's OP, it's quite simple.
When sales die down, they'll nerf it, so that way, the next content can be OP, without having to be OP over the currently OP things.
Highly reccomended.

After playing through it the first time (taking 27 hours), I can safely say I see the reason why a lot of people liked it when it came out and still like it now. Though personally, I'm a much bigger fan of Borderlands 2, this is still a really fun and solid game to play.
The only problems I had were occasional issues with rendering background details, huge frame drops, and all of the frame tearing that could ever exist. Seriously, it was horrible. I got used to it, but that's not something I should have to get used to. There was also no option to adjust render distance, and even with re-downloading the game, I had persistent problems with rendering all background animations. I also had to run the game on a lowered resolution (1366x768) to get these premium-status bugs/glitches. If I ran the game on 1080p w/ any settings adjustments, it got worse, and it stayed below 25 fps.
The game mechanics, however, were fairly simply and not hard to get used to. I had quite a bit of fun with the battle sequences of fighting Rakk, Skags, Bandits,
, and
. All guns were simple to use, so there's nothing too special there aside from the several million variations they arrive in. And the legendary weapons. And the cyan/pearlescent weapons. And the
.
All in all, I'd say that this game was worth the money, and is certainly fun to play. Humor could use a touch-up (what humor there is is either really funny, weak, or obscene), and the character face animations and all character movements (whether it be player or NPC) could've been better, but the plot itself is good and the game is fun to play. This game could've been better, but it was already good in it's own regards. I mean, it's not Borderlands 2.

although it says i have only 425 hours in this game that is far from the truth, i found this game on its website and then i went and found it on steam. Now although i love this game i will try to not be bias. so to begin, i will start the pros and then go to the cons
PROS:
1.this game is massive, as of Thursday October 30, 2014. there is 16 generation story lines . then there is two episodic story lines , saga and iria, with iria on its 4th episode.
2. you can do almost anything in this game. I always ask people " tell me what you'd like to do in the game." and I normally get stuff like "trading, clothing crafting, black-smithing " and those exist , probably one of the only things you cant do is open pvp. you have to invite the person to a pvp battle and they have to accept it.
3. the graphic style, now this is both a pro and a con, i will talk about the pro part here, the good thing about the graphics is that they are rather simple. now not to say the game looks boring. the areas you can go are diverse and interesting. a winter mountain range full of giants, or a desert in a constant sandstorm with elves. or do you go to the lands of tera and tailliann, the front of the fight in g9
4. skill "tree". this game offer a interesting system for skills. it is free flowing. everything if offered to you at the start, there are a few that you have to unlock( like meteor, blizzard, and hydra transformation) or you have to be good in one skill set to unlock hidden skills. the beauty of the system is that you can always be doing stuff. i have one character that is level 2500 total and i have barely mastered any skill sets.
5. Combat, now combat is interesting because it truly matters on what skill set you choose to adopt. a battle mage or spell sword are going to fight completely differently from an archer or puppeteer. but the most basic combat is like a real time rock paper scissors where some skills trump others but are trumped by others. this makes you require a bit of strategy but also quick moves
6. events, there are always really fun and entertaining events, just last summer their was a big staged event that ended with an SAO event
Cons.
1. camera control, now this is the biggest complaint I've gotten from people, the camera is not the easiest to control. you ether have to right click, or move you mouse to the side of the screen. now yes in combat it can be a bit annoying. but it just takes a getting used to, it takes a bit of pre-planning
2.graphics, like i said this is a pro and a con, now if you like the style and since its low in the graphics you can easily play it on low end pcs, but if you have a better one or don't like the art style, it will definitely be a turn off.
3. the openness, now i know a lot of people like the openness but most likely as a newbie will get so caught up will all the possible skills he will want to try to use all of them and be weaker than they need to fight enemies of there level. it takes a bit of discipline to focus on just one class.
4. pay-to-winness, now this may not be noticed by most people but since it is a free to play, there has to be some form of transactions. some of those include cool pets (like dragons) or gachapon that hold special items. these are used to get special items, these items can then be sold for gold to other players to make a profit. yes this does happen, yes there are people who have a whole quick slot full of dragons. but because of those people, everything can be acquired in game for gold. now it might annoy people that this is true but pay to win is not entirely true. it just depends what your term for "winning" i can honestly say I've probably spent 500+ on this game and that might sound crazy but for how many hours I've clocked i think its worth it

I recommend the game, but with the condition that you should only get it if you know what you're getting into. Only get it if you want to support this game's development, which is a worthy cause, and if you understand that this isn't a finished game and that it won't be finished for quite some time. Okay, I'm gonna go straight to the point here. I love the concept that this game has. I think the fact that you can rebirth and master multiple skills instead of being restricted to one class is really cool. Being a music teacher, I also love how you can compose music on here using actual music theory. The in-game music is pretty awesome as well. One thing I don't like is how buggy the game is. The pathwaying for the game seems pretty sloppy, as I occasionally find myself glitching in the same spot when I try to talk forward (especially through the narrow hallways in the dungeons). I also invited some friends to play the game, and it seems like most of them have problems when they try to launch it (these people also have very capable computers, so I wouldn't call it a systematic problem). Another thing that really bothers me is the pop-up tip windows. I try disabling them, but it doesn't seem to work. It's tediously annoying to have to deal with that appearing in the middle of my screen during a fight.
Overall, I like this game. I think you'll enjoy it too, if you can work around the little annoying bugs and pop-up windows.

UPDATE: Original "review" at the bottom of the current one
It's been a little more than 2 years since I posted my original "review" for Proteus, and looking back I must say it was hardly a proper overview of this game. Just some loose, short and rather ambiguous opinions of the overall product as a whole, hardly anything constructive or informative, something that is unfortunately quite common in the review section, but it is definitely no excuse for producing a rather poor piece of writing regarding this particular product (even if I'm not a journalist, I should have tried harder). The problem is, that this type of game doesn't really suit me and does not match my preferences, something I didn't know before I tried it, and since I was unable to gain enjoyment out of this, I felt somewhat salty and decided to leave unfavorable opinion.
I can definitely say that the graphics are really nice,and although they are simplistic, I think they are the perfect choice for this kind of game, because of their charm and the fact that they go extremely well with the soundtrack, that is dynamic and changes depending on what happens on the screen. But unfortunately this is how I perceive this game: simple (though pleasant) graphics accompanied by the appropriate, everchnaging soundtrack, and the only one can do is to explore the procedurally generated island, something that I, personally, wasn't captivated by and ultimately didn't enjoy. In the end, if I were to summarize my whole experience I would say that "It isn't my cup of tea."
If you are considering the purchase of this game, I hope my thoughts can be of some use, maybe as another point of view, though I highly encourage you to read other reviews, as others explored the features of this game more extensively. And if you enjoyed this game, I must say that I am envious that it met your expectations, though I'm glad it did, as at the end of the day this is the most important part of all the gaming: to have fun.
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
While the idea is interesting, and the soundtrack is quite relaxing, "Proteus" gets boring really quick. The only thing player can do, is to walk around and observe the rather empty scenery. Seven euros is way too much for this game. To be honest, it doesn't deserve even half of the asked price.

Atom Zombie Smasher is my favorite game, so far, to come from Blendo Games. They are a quirky game company so their games can be a mixed bag but that's very okay because they are not afraid to try new things and think outside of the box. Atom Zombie Smasher mixes RTS, tower defense, and a bit of turn based strategy. The object of the game is to rescue civilians from cities that are under zombie attack. While rescuing them, you fend off the zombies with mercenary teams that you acquire throughout the campaign. You also have to try to capture cities and strategically select cities to rescue to help stop the spread of the zombies. It's kind of like the board game, Pandemic, mixed with some tower defense. The visuals in this game are very simplistic. People and zombies are represented by cubes. It may seem like a silly decision but it actually helps to maintain a fun atmosphere to the game to have colorful cubes running around the city. Most zombie apocalypse games have dark and gritty atmospheres to create a horror setting. You won't find that here. Atom Zombie Smasher is all about the strategy and the frantic game-play. Add a "Christmas" mini-game, co-op, and mod support and you've got a great game.

One of my top twenty games of the last few decades . . . when it works. It is really addictive, twitchy strategy, and you have more choice than you might realize when you set up a game -- you can choose whether you want random mercs for a greater challenge, or choose your teams, or add options to make it even harder, and a longer or shorter game may grant you more victories based on your play style. If you're frustrated, just change the options. Cute story, kind of nonsensically artsy, think Monty Python surrealism as told by Quentin Tarantino.
That being said, it can be kinda tricky to set up to run in the first place -- you might not have any problems, but based on your system, you may also sit there for an hour trying out different graphics and launch options through the forums and the dev FAQ before it runs, or before you can actually see the whole screen. Be patient, it's worth it, you'll probably get it running, but be prepared that you may need to figure out how to launch it. Not DOS-game hard to set up, but requiring more persistence than most modern games.

Now let me start off my review by saying that this isn't a game for casual players. If you want to mash some buttons and get through stuff alright you're gonna get frustrated and angry.
People who have played Gothic and previous Risen games will feel right at home here though.
The game is in many ways an improvement over Risen 2, I'll sum up all the points I think have been improved over compared to the previous game in the franchise.
+ Much bigger world
+ Tons of quests and things to do
+ Combat at sea against sea monsters (ripped from Assassins Creed Black Flag but still nice)
+ 3 different factions to join (exactly like in gothic 2, you can pick one and stuff will change according to your choice)
+ Magic is back, there are tons of spells and skills for you to learn (Voodoo is back and awesome!)
+ Treasure searching from Risen 2 is back in force and theres a lot of stuff for you to find
+ Companions have more to say and aren't just there like in Risen 2, the game feels more alive. (They give you advice and sometimes really save your life during fights)
+ Less bugs and glitches than in Risen 2 (although there are still a few minor issues)
+ Gorgeous evironments! (Seriously, look at some screenshots!)
+ Music and sound is perfect!
+ Replayablility because of the 3 different factions (You can only join one of them so you can play the game again and experience it in a different way with different skills and everything!)
+ Hilarious dialog sometimes
+ Feels a lot like gothic! (no, seriously it does. The 3 different factions you can join and the overall feel of the game when you're playing is very similar. You even get good references to gothic sometimes throughout the game. Scavengers are in the game and there's a guy called Moe asking for money in front of the tavern :D and those are just a few of them.)
+ Did a quest for a parrot, got 2200 gold and new armor! (10/10)
Unfortunately there are a few things that just aren't that good...
I love the game but in order to make this an honest game review I gotta put the negatives here too.
- Voice acting is a mixed bag (For me it was fine but other players will think it's horrible)
- Armor is really scarce throughout the game, you'll get your faction armor when you join one of them but that's about it.
(It was pretty much the same in the gothic games though)
- The game has frame rate issues
- Enemy AI is horrible sometimes
- ocasional pop in throughout the entire game
- Some graphical glitches here and there
- Clothes of npc's don't look that great sometimes (clipping)
- Combat is challenging in the gothic kind of way, in the beginning you'll have to run away from enemies sometimes. If you wander off and go to deep in some parts of the islands you'll encounter monsters that are way to strong for you. Levelling is slow at first but once you're strong the game is a lot of fun. Gothic was the same and if someone says it isn't they're lying. I've finished Gothic 1 and 2 for like 3 times so I know how the games are. I don't have a problem with this but others will, thats why I said at the beginning that this isn't for casual players.
Overall the game was and still is a lot of fun for me, I'll probably keep playing it for a while like I did with Risen 2. But players that aren't used to this kind of gameplay wont enjoy it as much as I did. I'm sure of that, so my advice to those people would be to play Gothic 2 or try out Risen 2. If you get annoyed as hell and hate the levelling and the overall gameplay of those 2 this isn't the game for you. It doesn't do anything new or inovative, it's made for the fans of those 2 franchises
