In Scarlett Mysteries: Cursed Child you play as Scarlett Everitt, a paranormally gifted woman on the search for her father who left her at an orphanage to keep her safe. A letter of his leads her to a train station and she gets drawn into the mystery of another cursed child.
Her psychic abilities come into play twice. First you have the clues of your father which act as this game's collectibles. There are 29 of them and they sometimes turn invisible for a few seconds. There's no backtracking in the game though, so always look out for them. Second you have Scarlett's visions, which act as a memory of the past and can be entered via a little puzzle. Some visions are just a clip to reveal a clue, but some allow you to go back in time as another person and reenact the situation. Basically you play a few sceneries again in the past.
The problem with the game is that it has barely any hidden object puzzles and it takes a while to even get to the first one. You also won't find a lot of minigame puzzles, but I think most hidden object games don't offer a lot of them.
There are no repetitive achievements and it's the first hidden object game I've played that didn't have you play on the hardest difficulty for another achievement. It's also short and doesn't have a bonus chapter. It's a good length for a lazy afternoon, but you'd probably expect a bit more content for that price.
Overall it's a beautiful and modern game, but as a hidden object game it kinda fails. I'd recommend the game for new players who want to ease into the genre or old players who are only bothered by bad puzzles and bad stories.

Scarlett Mysteries is an effortlessly easy hidden object game with a clumsy, but still wonderfully charming little story.
Scarlett Mysteries: Cursed Child is a perfect example of a super casual hidden object game—a game that provides next to no challenge. Its puzzles are a bit rare in HOGs, but they always provide an obvious solution. The items in the hidden object scenes are large and distinguishable. Finally, the point ‘n’ click parts are held in check by splitting the game into several chapters, all of which have 3-4 screens as the current playing area.
While the gameplay is very lightweight, the story, interestingly, is a bit darker than expected. We play as a young medium who is searching for her lost father but stumbles upon a family drama instead, where she has to rescue the daughter of a rich factory owner from a seemingly vengeful spirit.
What is surprising regarding this story is that it should not be enjoyable. The dialogues are silly, the voice acting is soulless, and the plot stumbles around all the time… yet there is something so inherently charming in it that somehow it fits the gameplay like a glove.

This one is for all the gamers interested in trying EVE out. I'm about 100 hours, 3 weeks in.
I might as well get this out of the way:
EVE really isn't a video game. It's more of a second, virtual life.
It's notorious for being difficult and having a steep learning curve, and as a life-long gamer (super nintendo days), I think that's pretty much true. It's information overload in the first few days of play. That being said, CCP and the EVE community have done their best to make the game accessible and playable to the average gamer. The tutorials are decent, and there are a multitude of FAQs, wikis, reedits and youtube videos on the web for those looking and willing to learn more about the game. It's a game of patience, but it can also be really fun.
It's a sandbox, so you get what you want out of it. EVE has gotten some mainstream coverage for its epic fleet battles (at 4 FPS, mind you), but that's really only one aspect of the game. As a player you can explore, mine, hunt pirates, go to war, trade, build etc. It's really up to you: if you want to be a lonewolf and never have to interact with anyone, you can do that. If you want to join a corporation (clan) and do things with other people, you can do that as well.
EVE is obviously a very well-made game, but I think the real gem behind its success is that it has one of the most supportive gaming communities in the world. Sure, there are always going to be trolls, but from my experience so far, a significant number of players in EVE are genuinely nice people, who enjoy and love the game and are willing to help noobs out (though they will not hesitate to blow your ship up, given the chance). I can't stress how refreshing and cool that is.
As for the costs, don't worry about the subscription too much. It can be paid for via in-game money, which you earn by doing stuff in the game such as missions etc. If you really want to play this game for free, all it takes is some time.
If you bypass steam, there's currently a 14-day free trial on EVE's own site. Try it out. If it's for you, it's for you.

Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 3 Full Burst is the latest installment in the Ultimate Ninja series. After years of listening to the incredible stories being egenerated by Eve, yet never being able to see how they matched up with an incredibly complicated-looking front end I finally gave this gem the time it deserved.
Is it very complicated? Yes, very! However giving the game time to explain itself to you, contacting the various player-run corporations and receiving help and training makes the learning curve more of a gentle slope than a cliff.
What is enjoyable about it? Well firstly it looks incredible, its software and graphics have been updating to keep up with modern hardware and the game runs beautifully and looks even better. Secondly the combat is so very tactical that you really can't get a feel of how complex combat scenarios are until you are in command of one, ie try it! Thirdly you have the sandbox. Full-blown economic sandbox with empires rising and falling, constant conflict and intrigue within the massive playerbase. Simple put: Fun and satisfying combat along a large-scale universe-wide simulation.
Progression?
Contrary to how it looks, progression is measured in the skills your characters learns. These skills are learned in real-time whether you are on or offline. You need to always be learning something! Ships are bought and lost, but yuor characters remains permanent (well, sometimes he gets a little roughed up..).
PVE?
Yes, and the majority of your early days will be spent doing some fairly enjoyable and in-depth PVE missions. There is enough content here to play the game only as PVE.
Go and try it out, you will not regret it.

Atom Zombie Smasher is a simple, yet fun, game about zombies and controlling flow. In it's own way it is very much a simple puzzler.
The game is divided into two areas. First there is the overworld map where land is divided into provinces for you to contest over with the zombie menace. Here you choose which area to send your mercenaries to infected provinces of varying difficulty (number of infected present) and, depending on the game settings you chose, choosing which mercenaries to send. Second is the battle map itself. Here you get to place where your rescue chopper will initally land and draw survivors towards it as well as other mercenaries in building around the map (artillery, snipers, etc) or deployed in the streets (foot soldiers, mines, dynamite, barricades, etc).
Mercenaries are all designed to help you control flow and rescue survivors and scientists from the infected zones. Helicopter for rescue, artillery, foot soldiers, snipers, barricades, mines and dynamite are all examples of some of the mercs you get to use. As you attain kills or successful rescue numbers each merc group will level up and be upgradeable. This generally comes down to faster movement, rate of fire, deployment or reduced loading times.
As the game progresses and you rescue more scientists you gain control of the 'Llama Cannon" which allows for orbital bombardment of a zone every few provinces.
All in all the game is fun and can be addictive depending on your tastes.
Pick this up in a sale and you certainly won't regret it!

Gunpoint is a film noir-inspired puzzle game by indie developer Tom Francis. The game consists of a variety of puzzles that are solved using your crosslink, a handy hacking device that you use to rewire doors, buttons and other assorted mechanisms. These puzzles are weaved together by an excellent story. You play as Richard Conway, a detective who is out to clear his name after being framed for murder. The music in this game is phenomenal. The soundtrack consists of many jazz tracks, most of which are remixed in a more techno-esque fashion. I 100% completed the game in 7.4 hours, including all achievements and A+'s in all the levels. The final level of the game is one of the best in any game ever, providing an extremely satisfying ending. My only complaint is that the game is a tad short, but this could be easily solved by a story-expanding DLC release.
OVERALL RATING: 9.5/10

I wanted to love this game, truely, I did. The game is and can be fun, but there are just moments that just make the entire experience frustrating and draining.
I'll get into that later, but first, I want to get into what makes this game great. The first, is what is advertised is that you can play your way, and that is true! You want a tank? go make a badass tank; want a walker or mech? Sure you can have that; How about a car? or a helicopter/aeroplane raining hell from above? Yup, it is all there and how you approach it is entirely up to you, and this is one of the few games where creativity can be rewarded. Everytime I go into a new match there is usually that pair of creative players with whacky designs that are full of suprises.
Yes your chosen robot can and probably will have design flaws that can be exploited. The free to play aspect ruins this further however, when you are forced to "buy" or "roll" for parts that you need to correct these flaws or make your robot competitive. To be fair, the game makes it easy to get loot crates and currency. You can get dozens and dozens of parts just by playing for a few hours. However, t  get the most out of your time, you're gonna need premium, which is rather inexpensive for just a few days and theres even an option for permanent premium, a company that gives that option is one that gets respect from me.
But I still can't recommend the game. That reason stems from how the game is balanced in terms of weapons and in some cases, match making.
What really makes me question match making though, were two seperate matches I had where one team was nearly all aircraft, and the other team was ground or air, but half of them had flak cannons. Weapons that get massive bonuses against flying targets. It was fairly obvious how those two games played out.
This brings me onto weapons themselves. How parts generally work in this game, is that the more rare the component or weapon is, the larger and more powerful it is. However, there sometimes an odd middleground where a rare or epic weapon packs just as much punch  at greatly reduced bulk or CPU cost. This is mostly in reference to Plasma Cannons and Rail Guns. I've seen far too many games where someone just packs the maximum for one or the other, and just outright annilates you. The killing blow for this game is that you don't have a chance to do anything cause your weapons have been blown off and/or your robot has been crippled cause your propulsion is compromised.
I can accept defeat or being outplayed, but there is no fun to be had when all your means of fighting back or fleeing are outright destroyed before you even realize whats going on.
Despite all my ranting, this is still a fun game. But its not a game I would recommend investing a ton of time or money into. But it's free, so no harm in trying it to see how you like it.

As a veteran who has played this game for 6-years, I would recommend this; however, this game has really reached its end-point and it has lost its luster. Why? There are various reasons and it's the reasons why I have left this game permanently, with some very few exceptions of coming back for the story content.
NOTE: I have played more than 2000+ hours of this game; however, I have never kept it attached to my current Nexon Account, because the one attached to this is my banned account.
Gameplay / Game Compatibility - The game engine runs on a pretty old engine from 2003 and it has hardly been tweaked for newer contents. While that might not be the problem, the reason why this game has issues here is because of the "security programs" and constant "bug fixes" that Nexon does. This game literally burnt out my previous computer, because it couldn't handle Nexon's new "security programs" and "fixes" between year 4 and 5, and had to buy an Alienware M14xR2 to keep playing at 30+ FPS a second. I can play Tera Online and Archeage and sustain better FPS at high graphics (which has a newer engine and better graphics) than what Mabinogi can do.
Game Management - Horrible. DO NOT HAVE HIGH STANDARDS FOR THIS COMPANY AT ALL OR YOU WILL BE DISAPPOINTED. This company has went back on many of its promises to the player base in the past few years and literally doesn't investigate problems appropriately. There are hackers still playing who has been in major incidents for several years, while there has been countless innocent players banned because Nexon found them for "illegal third-party clients." Even I was one of these victims in year 4 of my gameplay, but I just remade my character after months of trying to dispute the claim with their e-mail and ticket system.
Game Community - You can say this has the equalivency to Gaia Online. Dramatic, horrible, and down-right vile. While there might be a small group of players who actually are nice and look out for each other, the grand majority of the community is compiled of either: elitists, drama wh*res, fashion addicts, merchants, Nexon / Sabina whiteknights (people who solely defend Nexon with complete disregard of what wrong they've done), PvP addicts, pr*stitutes/womanizers, and/or trolls. I've played on three of the four servers and I can safely assume this is on all the servers.
Game Events - Hallowed out and barely worth it. Out of the all events in two years, there is about 5~10% of the events that we actually get rewarded with decent stuff. Otherwise, all the events that get transferred from the Korean/Chinese/Japanese Servers get their rewards hallowed out and replaced into the gachapon / boxes. This is the only way how they can actually sustain their game services, because they literally advertise the hell out of gachapons and any event that requires you to spend money. (Basically, Pay2Win) So, you're basically feeding the company money for decent-quality events in the game. While they might've removed rebirth cards and such, they still ♥♥♥♥♥ out the gachapons and other services like crazy. Teamwork vs. Solo - In the beginning, the game was heavily relied on Teamwork in the dungeons. I do quite enjoy this game if nothing but for the multi-player aspect of it and the ease at which my friends who aren't big into fighting games can grasp the mechanics and actually enjoy playing. This game isn't the greatest by any means, far from it, as a lot of things are missing that would make it just stellar.
We could do with more playable Dragonball Z characters. There were some that were just completely discarded from roster that are apart of the main story and that is just sad. No they aren't unlockable, they're just not there. Even if you bought the season pass this game will still be missing characters.
Missions and general story content are quite lacking. The fully voiced over story along with the occasional animation and awesome in game graphics are great and all, but there needs to be more, and the season pass isn't going to save this game from it's short term lifespan if they take their time releasing 3 missions at a time. As of right now I have only 2 open slots for characters to be made with the rest being filled with level 80's. This has taken almost no time at all and the only reason I have as much play time on this game as I do, is 1) drop rates, 2) drop rates, and 3) dragonballs. Everyone knows the drop rates are abysmal, but that's part of how this game is trying to keep itself alive.
Character creation is good, simple and fast. You never spend a whole lot of time dilly-dallying with this feature, but it has it's drawbacks. The biggest of which is that Humans and Saiyans all have exactly the same skins (hair, eyes, body types, clothes, etc.) and that other races are quite frankly, bland and lacking their own variety. With all of the countless races we've seen in both Dragonball and Dragonball Z over the years, you'd think that we could have some more variety when it came to races and even each individual races customization.
Power variety is there, but this being an RPG of sorts, you primarily tend to go for the powers and abilities that do the most damage and offer the most survivability. It's impossible not to min/max in this game. The lack of customization of these powers aside from picking and choosing is another let down. I love using final flash, or spirit bomb, or whatever, but why can't I assign a color scheme to them at the very least? It wouldn't be that big of a feature to add and would allow so much more personalization for players.
Transformations. Why only Super Saiyan? Seriously. Hurray for Kaioken, but ♥♥♥♥ that power. I made a Friezan soley for the purpose of being able to change forms into something awesome. No unlock potential for Humans or Nameks. No crazy alter ego's for Buus. Just Super Saiyan...and it wouldn't be so bad if Super Saiyan wasn't the bee's knees. Unlimited special attacks? Sign me right the ♥♥♥♥ on up.
Game Dev: "Here's 3 other race--"
Me: "No thanks! I'm good right here."
Game Dev: "But each race has it's own bonuses. Like the Nameks who have stretchy arms and suck at everything. Or the Majin who have less stretchy arms and suck only slightly less than Nameks because they have powers only they can use. Or the Friezan who...well...they punch good? Have a single ki blast that stuns and takes forever to shoot? Ummm, look cool?"
Me: "Ya I'll take genertic appearance and all that for unlimited special attacks. Sure I may not have passive health recovery, or a slightly larger health pool or stamina pool or passively regenerate ki like the Humans, but I do have the the ability to turn Super Saiyan and just spam Ultimate attacks until the cows come home."
This game is still good, don't get me wrong, but it could have been so much better, and for the price tag it could have been a lot better. Hold out until this game comes out on sale and then pick it up.

Dragon Ball Xenoverse is not a perfect game, but it's probably the best Dragon Ball Z game we've got right now.
The combat is simple, and fairly easy to learn. Each button corrosponds to a single action (light attacks, heavy attacks, ki blasts, etc) with little to no need to string together complex button presses or move the control stick around to do combos, sort of like a hack-and-slash game. You've also got Special moves (all of which cost 100 Ki) you can do using the same buttons while holding down the left trigger, and a couple Ultimate skills (costs 300 Ki) and an Evasive skill (costs 300 Stamina) that can be used the same way, just while holding down both triggers. Over all, combat is simple and easy to learn, but still manages to be fun, especially when it comes to mix-and-matching skills on your characters to see what works well together.
The story isn't too special, but in a way, it also kind of is. Most Dragon Ball games have us play through the same story that we all know and love, maybe with a few details changed around. But overall, it's still usually the same story. This game doesn't quite do that: Instead, Dragon Ball Xenoverse's story sort of picks up important things from the now-defuct Dragon Ball Online, an MMO with a lot of original ideas that didn't get to last long enough to see them properly executed. The Time Patrol returns, and your character is one of them, having been summoned by Trunk's wish on the Dragon Balls for a warrior who can help him fix up the timeline. Yes, you're exploring the story of DBZ... sort of, but the point this time is that critical moments in the story have been changed, and your job is to fix these continuity errors by correcting the outcome of battles that Towa and Mira have used their magic to change. An interesting twist that allows for newer elements without leaving the classic characters and settings behind.
Everyone gets to create their own original character for the game to use as their avatar for the HUB world and story quests, and there's a pretty good amount of customizability for your character. There are a number of races, all with their own distinct strengths, and even a character's sex makes a small difference, encouraging the player to make multiple characters to try out all the different combinations. Your character can also equip virtually every technique and article of clothing you could think of. Want to be able to use Hercule's Dynamite Kick and Freiza's Death Beam at the same time? You can do that. As long as you're willing to work for it, you can get it for your character, and there are very few limits as to what kind of character can equip what kind of skill. Your imagination really is king, here.
... Or at least it would be, if not for one little factor: The RNG. There's a large random factor to a few things in the game (NPC location, drop rates for skills and equipment, etc.) in the game, and it's far from generous. The drop rates in this game are quite stingy, and the missions are typically fairly long unless you are grossly over-leveled, so going through a 5-to-15 minute quest, only to not get anything out of it, can be annoying, especially if it happens multiple times in a row. Sadly, the rank you score on a mission doesn't really seem to affect drop rates, only how much EXP you get. Thankfully, EXP gains are pretty generous, especially if you rank high on a mission, so leveling up is fairly quick. You're likely to level up ever other mission you do, as long as its level and yours match up evenly enough. Each mission also has multiple "stages" to it that can be unlocked if you complete certain tasks within the mission in a specific way. However, these tasks aren't made clear to the player, and even if the player does everything right, it's still random as to whether or not the game thinks it counts, meaning you can do everything perfectly as the game wants you to, and still not get an Ultimate Finish based purely on luck.
My opinion on the audio is... complicated. The voice acting is generally good, but there are enough lines that have been mistranslated, or have the wrong audio play every time the line comes up, that the issue can't be ignored. Cutscenes are also much louder than gameplay, which, save for the sound effect (which are way too loud by default), are fairly quiet. The game also has a tendency to stop the battle music if you back off from an enemy for more than 4 seconds, even if you're still fighting them and are just trying to get some distance, which can ruin the moment.
Back to gameplay issues again, the enemy AI has a tendency to outright cheat (knocking you out of moves that have full super armor with a single Ki blast, any character who goes Super Saiyan stays Super Saiyan forever, dodging attacks and grabs that clearly connect with them, etc.), while your partner AI is generally dumber than a sack of rocks. Sometimes, they're outright liabilities. If you can, try to do Parallel Quests with friends; You get more competent partners, and it's more fun than playing alone! Everyone wins!... as long as there isn't a connection issue. Then things might get a bit laggy, or someone may have to disconnect.
Ultimately, Dragon Ball Xenoverse is a game that does well when it comes to its core concepts and mechanics, but little things like issues with the AI, the RNG being a bigger deciding factor than it needs to be, and the occasional connection problem with the server, prevent it from being as good as it could be. And these are all things that could be fixed with some patches fairly easily. It's a good game that gets held down by small problems that pop up often enough to prevent it from reaching its full potential.
tl;dr: If you're a fan of Dragon Ball Z, you'll probably love this game, but may be frustred by its small problems and how much presence they have. Still, I would recommend this game, because the good really does outweigh the bad.

This was a pretty stellar game. I have played this off and on over the last couple years, lol....but that is no indictment on the game. Actually, my interest in both the topic and the LEGO aspect kept bringing me back, even though my gamer ADD often took hold. The humor added to a mostly dark adventure was perfect, and as somebody who knows the LOTR inside and out, I really appreciated all the subtle jokes and such. Often, they really said what a lot of fans were thinking. The gameplay itself is fairly standard LEGO game fare. Engaging and simple enough that anybody can pick up this game and play it through to its conclusion. I also like how they broke the game up into three books with credits at the end of each. That was appropriate IMO.
The extras such as free roam and so on all are also what you would expect and could literally add countless hours to your game.
My only complaint is that a played a couple chapters offline, and the game never synced those trophies afterwards, so it is kind of odd seeing my completion without some of the end of chapter achievements (like the Weathertop one for example).
All in all, I would consider this a must own for LOTR and/or LEGO game fans. Very well done. Let's see, 16 rings of power out of 19 possible with one ring to rule them all.

If you're going into this completely blind, you should know this is not just another Borderlands game. This is a Telltale-styled adventure game set in the Borderlands universe. Rather than collecting loot and shooting faces, you will be primarily making on-the-fly dialog choices to direct the scenes how you want to see them play out. You don't have to have played any past Borderlands games to enjoy the experience, but you will get more out of it if you have. Especially Borderlands 2.
With that out of the way, this game was really well done. The writing and voice acting were both great and really brought the characters to life. It's a shame that Telltale hasn't found a way to evolve their gameplay beyond constant QTEs, but it didn't get in the way very often. At least you don't have to feel too pressured about permanently losing characters due to your QTE performance like in some other games in the genre. Comparatively, this game is more humorous and light-hearted in tone. Overall, it's a really fun ride with a few heartstring pullers near the end. I would certainly recommend this game to just about anyone.

The last great standing Titan from the old school original MMO's.
E.V.E Online is a shining example of what an MMO can be. It has the deep skill and trait system with the open sandbox modern MMO's lack out right or fail to achieve in execution. Its well rounded and got a very social and skilled community. It's still going incredibly strong given its age and the Developers work tirelessly to add in new content on a shocking huge basis. They are keeping large aspects of it updated with modern gaming as well. Not over looking any aspect of their game engine. Its one huge server fitting 10,000+ daily average active players with little to no-lag.
E.V.E Online is space based Pvp at its best. Yes, There are no manual dog fighting FPS style controls here but once you get used to their control system you will notice that less and less as you get drawn into the E.V.E gameplay. E.V.E works on a traditional stat and trait system not all that disimilar from older MMO's like SWG (Pre-C.U/NGE). This mix of skills and traits combined with your ship, ships bonuses and the equipment you choose to slot effects what kind of role you decide to play.
Needless to say the many menus, massive game map, dozens of factions, ratings, reputation let alone the controls are pretty staggering at first. But you eventually find yourself growing comfortable with them.
In E.V.E Online you can really do anything you can think of if you work hard enough at it. Are you the lone gun for hire jumping from system to system looking for work? Maybe your a power hungry warlord after total galactic domination? Or maybe your a Bounty Hunter searching for that right sum to retire on. The options in E.V.E Online are pretty vast and there is definately somthing for everyone.
E.V.E Online has been around for 11 years and counting now and has never lost its momentium and I'm sure it will be around for many many years to come.
E.V.E Online 11/11.

Personally, I do not like Mabinogi.  It has a lot of promise buried some where deep within it, but it never really appears.
The story you experience in the game consistently has you helping NPCs you'd rather brutally murder.  And the quests tied to these stories have various levels of imbalance, either being way too easy for a long time, or way too cheap all of a sudden causing you to die like crazy.
Although the game gives an impression that you can choose what skills you want to learn, what race you want to be, what equipment you want to wear, and what you want to do, you quickly learn that, in order to be good at the game, these choices quickly stop being choices.  Due to Combat Power requirements that only get worse as you level up and learn skills, you practically have to learn the skills in a set manner, with the most gruelling and reviled of these coming first simply because your lower Combat Power makes them "easier".  The races are imbalanced, with Elves being the butt monkeys of the game, Humans not really excelling at any one thing, and Giants being "teh best evarz".  Equipment is heavily restricted by Race and Gender, with the best either being horrendously ugly or costing an in-game fortune because they were once cash-shop items that you can no longer get.  And, as for doing what you want, you have the choice of pretending this is a fancy chatroom like Second Life or you have to do almost everything permanent, including the story, to become skilled at the game.
Of course, this game also has problems with lag and latency.  Regardless of how fast your connection is or how good your computer is, you will find yourself getting cheaped on by enemies you should be owning because they have consistent 0 lag and erratic movement while the game's engine is struggling to display certain graphics or send commands at a reasonable rate.  This hinderance continues as you will also occasionally to frequently miss the timing on certain skills, such as the Chain 2 and 3 Fighter skills, because the server starts the timer on them before it even sends the data to your client and you have to go through as series of back-and-forth messages with the client and server to line whatever skill you are trying to do to whatever enemy you are trying to do it on.
You might have better luck with the game than I did overall, but I'm just posting how I feel about the game.

Having suddenly been re-engulfed in this game to a greater extent than ever, I'll try to give better context to its staying power. Mabinogi is very rough around the edges, thanks in part to the localization being managed by Nexon of all things. It's over a decade old and much a product of its time, unoptimized, laggy, hard to get running on a modern OS, not very user friendly, the game does not explain itself well, you will constantly have to reference the wiki to make any headway in a number of things and understand the convoluted backend systems at work, Nexon support is nonexistent, and above all else the barrier to entry is horrible.
The way character progression works is by leveling up to gain "AP", which you use to rank up your skills that not only improve the skills' functionality, but often grant incremental stat bonuses. Then when the level grind gets too slow, you rebirth and start over from level 1 to continue accumulating AP. The end result is that the game is tailored around accumulating ridiculously inflated stat bonuses from skill ranks, to the point that your character level means little to nothing. Unfortunately, early quests are not very well balanced and have about as much chance of being a cakewalk as stoving your face in in an instant, as you are extremely fragile to start.
Where the game shines is in breadth of content. Combat is action-based and operates on a sort of rock-paper-scissors triangle that has since bloated outward but is still pretty interesting, on the rare occasion when it isn't being crippled by lag. Combat skill trees include swordplay, blunt weapons and axes, battle alchemy, magic, puppetry (yes, really), dual guns, one-on-one fisticuffs, archery, lancing, musical buffs and bludgeoning instruments, and for the hell of it, ninjas. Production skills include blacksmithing, fishing, cooking, mining, tailoring, herbalism, metallurgy, magic craft, engineering, carpentry, various alchemy, commerce, and for the hell of it, playing instruments via MML - the latter of which is what hooked my interest to begin with, actually.
If you're wondering where the payment incentive comes in, the answers are: pets, extra storage, and crappy lottery gachapons. Your starting inventory is pretty pithy all things considered; pets (that come with storage), special events, and limited edition cash shop items are the best remedy to this. Pets have the added bonus of being cute, and a semicompetent combat companion (if you level them up before they age).
So it's a bit hit and miss, but as a whole the game itself is a remarkable sight better than it once was, between all the retoolings and added content. It's still kind of a guilty pleasure, but a good romp with friends. If you ever play, be sure to set up on the Mari server. It's where all the cool guys are at.

The combat in this game is a lot of fun. I give it a 7/10 for the way it handles, though I have some minor nitpicks. Enemies tend to follow through with combos when you evade behind them, which often means you evaded for nothing. At least it feels that way for me. When an enemy falls to the ground, there doesn't seem to be a fast way to get to them to my knowledge. You can drop to the ground straight down, but if you need to approach them from a distance going down, it feels slower than going up or horizontal. I'm not sure why.
The story is nothing to write home about. Probably a 6/10 for me. It goes through all of the DBZ sagas and puts them in a "What If?" scenario where the villains are made stronger by some outside force. Some of the encounters in the main storyline felt unfair if you try them immediately after unlocking them. You're sometimes pit against 3 enemies at once, and when going after one, the other two attack from behind and stagger, making it rare to complete a combo or use a super attack effectively. I later learned that I'm supposed to grind Parallel Quests and old story quests to level up for some fights.
For instance, fighting against Frieza the first time, I was level 16 and getting my♥♥♥♥♥handed to me. After gaining a few levels from re-rurunning older missions, I beat him at level 21.
Another annoyance is that some enemies (most captain-y enemies like Ginyu or Vegeta) have a ki explosion that acts as a combo break. It hits in an AoE around them, does some damage, and makes them invincible for the duration of the animation. It wouldn't be too bad, but the animation for it is shorter than a quick attack. That also wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for the fact that these enemies have a habbit of spamming it any time you approach. I've had a fair share of fights against Ginyu where he used the break 4 times in a row. Sometimes they zoom up to you just to use the break. If you're not already guarding or far away, you're going to be hit by it.
The way stats work is fine. Another 6/10 aspect for me. It's nothing special, but if you spread your points too thin you're going to have a hard time in the game. You generally want to focus on either strike supers or blast supers, then either your ability spam evades with stamina or spam supers with ki, then the rest into health and attack. You can respec in the game, but you need to gather the dragon balls which can take a few hours of grinding.
The way you get abilities and gear in this game are garbage. 2/10, if even. When you complete a parallel quest, you have a chance at getting a piece of gear or super/ultimate attack (which supers/ultimates depends on which quest) when you defeat an enemy. You are not guaranteed anything. You can get duplicates of gear pieces, but once you learn an ability, you just have it. There's also a thing in these quests called Ultimate Finishes which trigger when certain criteria are met, like beating the mission within 5 minutes, or killing a certain enemy last. Some of these criteria have a
to proc, and some gear/abilities have a
to drop when that criteria is met.
Example: You must beat 3 guys, then 2 guys, then 3 more guys, but leave a specific guy for last. There is a chance that he will go super saiyan. This happens maybe 10-20% of the time. When you beat his super saiyan form, he has a chance to drop the ability to go super saiyan for your character. I got him to go super saiyan probably 20 times, and did not drop it. Luckily, this is one of the abilities you can buy from the skill shop for a bunch of zeni once you progress far enough into the story, but this is not the case for the vast majority of abilities.
Equipment stats are weird. You'll often get stuff that increases the damage your strike supers do, as well as your max ki and stamina, at the expense of your blast super damage. Meanwhile, other gear increases your blast super damage and health at the expense of your strike super damage and basic attack damage. Most of the early game clothes are zero-sum: +1 blast and health and -1 attack and strike. Later gear seems to start throwing it away for some play styles while keeping it in place for others. This is just an observation from the store clothes, as I haven't gotten a ton of quest gear drops.
The game is a lot of fun at first, then you hit the first brick wall and have to grind a bit to beat it. Then you hit the next brick wall and do the same thing. Then you have a close call or two but nothing that can't be handled. Then the final boss is a joke that can't damage you if you're not blind. Then you've completed the story and aren't at the level cap yet so all you have left is to spam parallel quests to get to level cap and have a chance at gear and abilities until the next set of quests comes out. Overall a 6/10, no real desire to play too much more once the story has been beaten, unless of course I'm going to play with someone else.

Wanted to at least beat the first level before reviewing.
Right now, this game is not even a dollar. For that price, I'm not expecting the level of art and creativity found here. For that, I have to commend it. However, with indie games/cheap games, there are often trade offs. You want a brilliant story? The gameplay might be weak. You want a great story and good gameplay? The graphics might be terrible.
So what's this game's trade off? Unfortunately, it's usability. The game is ***CUMBERSOME***
I'll briefly go down a list of pros, I'll be a bit more in-depth for the cons, then my closing thoughts.
Pros:
-Cheap
-Easy to get into
-Content
--Plenty of levels, heroes, loot, etc. to utilize, for the cheap price you're getting a lot
-Co-op
-No port forwarding nonsense needed
-Relatively active community/devs
Cons:
-Stuttering
--For such a simple game, I should not be stuttering so consistently. It's most often with a couple of enemies around, but sometimes it's just with a boss. It's quite ridiculous, really. This game should run 900 frames a second on a decent machine (which I have). I can understand with hoards upon hoards of enemies with explosions and other effects going on, but sometimes it's just a couple of rats
-Buggy
--The few bugs I've run into; invulnerable enemies that require my blood to be killable (if this is part of the game, something on screen would help, but one rat dies, its brother takes no damage, a little confusing). I've crashed twice trying to navigate the menus. I tried to lower the master volume, and the bar shot across the screen passed where I could actually click it. And yes, it raised the sound 500%. I had to start the game to get the master volume bar to be visible
-UI
--The game requires WASD or other key inputs to navigate. That's a big no no on PC games. Please make it so the mouse clicks are read on menu screens. You want to see how your helm compares to the new ones you looted? Well, wasd to get to the helmet. Then push F to compare your helmet to helmets in your inventory. Then wasd up and down the helmets you own, pushing F on each and every one because you can't actually see stats until you equip the item. Push G to get out of the helmets and check your chest pieces, weapons, whatever. Can get very confusing with multiple items of each, and it's not fast in the slightest which it sorta needs to be in this game. That's just an example though, I really do not like the UI in this game.
-Four directional limited attacks
--Seriously why can't I shoot diagonally?
-Melee seems incredibly unbalanced compared to the ranged heroes
--Bosses sometimes will one hit you on contact. Good luck being a melee character then. (THIS COULD BE DUE TO ME SUCKING AT THE GAME/NOT GETTING VERY FAR YET)
A lot of cons, a lot of pretty damning cons. However, the game is fun. I don't know what it is about it, perhaps it's how satisfying it is to go from shooting 30 damage arrows, to shooting 300, to shooting 3000. The satisfaction is real. I would easily recommend this game without the long list of cons. I still recommend it, I do have to warn any pondering buyers; this game is flawed. You're not exactly paying a lot so you can't expect a golden goose, but it's still worth mentioning.
If you have even 1 friend that wants to join, get this game. If you have more, it's a blast. Even with the stuttering, unbearable UI, and annoying lack of diagonal combat.

There are two very important things to note about this game that one should be aware of before investing their time and/or money into it. The good thing is the gameplay is great. It feels well done and exciting, the movement is responsive and fluid, and once you have the car or tank you want it is a really good time.
The bad news is that it's remarkably difficult to get said car or tank. If you want to earn the money needed to craft, (yes, this TOO has a crafting system) you have to use a market that doesn't work and is unreliable and there is no alternative to earning money. There is no way around it, either, because in order to craft anything useful you need to rent a workbench with said money. If you want to earn that money by selling the raw resources then be prepared for a 9-5 job that stops becoming a place for fun and becomes, again, a job.
If you want you can buy this money with REAL MONEY! Imagine that. A game that has a huge grind but you can cut it with real money. That doesn't sound pay to win. (It isn't P2W, but I'll get on that subject in a moment) And even if you do use real money you need a significant amount of spare cash, IRL cash, to get anywhere. So even if the game is truly fantastic with the vehicle you want, obtaining that vehicle is such a huge pain in the♥♥♥♥♥the fun is taken away, defeating the point of playing a game in the first place.
On the topic of P2W, the game isn't P2W. Pay To Win implies that there are things which are only available through real money investment that give you an advantage. (there are things like that which exist, but the market also has those things and they're not that special anyway.) What I think this game is would be more like P2P. You have to spend real money, and a fair bit of it, before you can enjoy the game in the first place. Winning is up to how well you can design your craft, but getting the parts is practically impossible without buying something.

This is a fun and addictive game. It looks fantastic, plays well, and is easy to learn.
You can get hours of enjoyment playing this Free to Play game if it is just wreaking havoc on the field or designing your death machine.
I will attempt to go over the Pros and Cons of this game.
---
Pros:
Easy interface.
Low learning curve.
Wonderful graphics.
Progression starts off quick and slows down in the higher levels.
A multitude of car parts and weapons, along with several paint schemes, that all fit nicely together to create your perfect terror machine.
No end to the crazy variations of vehicles you will encounter in game from other players.
Fast loading.
All items are available to the players via online purchases or "grinding".
Adequate number and variations of maps and play styles.
Ability to form clans to play with your friends.
---
Cons:
Building interface, right mouse click button can sometimes delete multiple parts at once.
Limited design and part storage with ability to upgrade via online purchase or "grinding".
"Grinding" takes forever. Resources are earn in very little amounts. Experience points are also earn in low amounts. Players are charged ingame credits for building parts, which cost resources already, by charging the player to "rent" a workbench in order to craft a part. Players are taxed on ingame part sales. This means the game takes a percentage of what you make on selling parts for no apparent reason. All parts sell for a ridiculously low amount. All high end weapons/parts cost a ridiculously high amount. Paint schemes are also extremely high in cost for no good reason at all. In order to have a high end machine with accompaning weapons, the player must "grind" for days on end in order to achieve just a portion of the amount it will take to build the parts. Or...you can just buy them with ingame credits. This also takes for ever to save up because most sales are for tenths of a credit, while most upgraded parts are in the tens of credits to hundreds of credits to even thousands of credits. You can always pay real money to purchase in game credits. And that is how they make their money. If you see a player with a super machine, they bought it. If they say different, they are lying.
Match making is based on a Power Score (PS).  This is calculated on the combination of parts. But the match making tolerance is something like +/- 1500. So, a player with a PS of 3200 can end up in a match with players ranking at 5400+. This means almost instant death to the 3200 player. Also, high end players can build a machine consisting of merely a frame and a cab and wheels ( which would be a very low PS ) and then add super weapons to it. Thus, keeping their PS low enough to enter matches with players that still have starter weapons.
Clans. The game matches are 8vs8, but you can only take four members of your clan in a match. You are force to play with strangers or bots if not enough players are in game. Even the clan battles only allow four members.
Drones. This is the game breaker here. Drones are a cancer to the game. Wheeled drones ( Sidekicks ) are armed with a "Spectre" heavy machine gun. This is an expensive weapon ( $350.00+ ingame credits ) to add to your machine. But drones cost $50.00 credits. So, for less than the price of one Spectre gun attachment, a player can buy four sidekick drones. That means four auto-aiming, fast moving, tiny vehicles are now running all around a player shooting perfectly into said player all at once. Before the player can even take out one ( if he notices they have been deployed in time ) his machine is ripped to pieces and is destroyed. This is a matter of seconds. And the player that deployed the drones merely drove near the other player, dropped, and ran away. Then collects the experience and points for that kill. All without ever having to engage a single player. And because they are relatively inexpensive and highly effective, they are in every match now. Most of the time with three to four opposing players with deploy vehicles ( imagine a brick with wheels, a design without any need to be creative, Just lay out a frame, add wheels, a cab, then line the rest with drone boxes. ).
Other super weapons and hovers ( aka floaters ). The damage and armor on the super high end equipment is quite unbalanced. You can spend most of the match trying to remove a single hover pod using blue or purple grade weapons and maybe get one off. But, those floaters typically are also carrying a super weapon or two or three and will destoy you in one shot. Or worse, the floaters fly quickly over your area, knocking any top mount weapons right off of your machine by running into it, then dropping four or more SIdekick drones which will then rip you to pieces.
The maps. There are approximately 10,000 places to get your machine stuck on any given map. Rocks. trees. Cracks in the road. If you are not careful, you could spend your entire time just trying in vain to get your vehicle unstuck. And of course, die before that happens.
---
My summary is that this game is a Pay to Win game. They disguise this by allowing the player to actually achieve possession of super items as long as they play hours on end, everyday, for weeks. Giving that they collect more than they need for any given part they wish to craft in order to sell the extra stuff off for credits. Because they will still need to "rent" a worspace.
It is easier and quicker to just dish out some real money for some ingame credits and buy the overpriced part.
I like game minus the cons. I had lots of fun in the beginning. When it was a battle between players in thier machines shooting it out. Now that I am in the higher levels, it is just a tedious battle to avoid getting shredded by a horde of drones that infest evey map.
So, at this time I am leaving a NO as a recommendation. I read that they "might" do something about the imbalance and drone problem. If they do fix these issues throughout development I will change my recommendation and alter my review to reflect those changes.
TL;DR version;
Fun at the beginning, pay2win drone spammers ruin the game later on.

If you're going into this completely blind, you should know this is not just another Borderlands game. This is a Telltale-styled adventure game set in the Borderlands universe. Rather than collecting loot and shooting faces, you will be primarily making on-the-fly dialog choices to direct the scenes how you want to see them play out. You don't have to have played any past Borderlands games to enjoy the experience, but you will get more out of it if you have. Especially Borderlands 2.
With that out of the way, this game was really well done. The writing and voice acting were both great and really brought the characters to life. It's a shame that Telltale hasn't found a way to evolve their gameplay beyond constant QTEs, but it didn't get in the way very often. At least you don't have to feel too pressured about permanently losing characters due to your QTE performance like in some other games in the genre. Comparatively, this game is more humorous and light-hearted in tone. Overall, it's a really fun ride with a few heartstring pullers near the end. I would certainly recommend this game to just about anyone.

This is purely a review of the HD edition.
The review is structured into the following parts:
1. Story 4/6
2. Gameplay 3/6
2.1 Singleplayer
2.2 Multiplayer
3. Graphics 4/6
4. Sound 4/6
5. Price
6. Summary and score
At the end of each part you see my personal rating. It is possible to score a maximum of 6 points for each part. Needlessly to say that more points are better. At the end these points will be calculated together for the final score.
Gameplay gets an overall score, and the price of the game gets no score.
1. Story: As far as I know the story of Age of Empires 2 is fairly accurate when it comes to what happened in the real world. So it is fair to say that the story is realistic and good. Furthermore, the narration of the Story is beautiful.
2. Gameplay
2.1 Singleplayer: I am not much of a skirmish player, so this will be mostly about the campaign. Instead of one big campaign that leads you through what happens in one country, Age of Empires 2 gives you the opportunity to play different races. This creates diversity and is therefore good. Furthermore, you don't need to play the campaign in a specific order, so if you want to, you can jump straight to Saladin's campaign. The missions are okay, some are a bit difficult but most of them are pretty easy with the right strategy. Overall the campaign keeps you busy and is fairly fun the only problem is that the maximum population is 200, which is definitely not enough for someone like me because you can't have a powerful economy and a mighty army at the same time.
2.2 Multiplayer: I am not a competitive PvP player at all when it comes to strategy games. I get easily frustrated and salty by certain tactics and can't multitask properly. So what I did was, grab a few friends and play compstomp. It may sound boring but it was fairly entertaining. Age of Empires 2 gives you plenty of opportunities to interact with your allies and thus makes this a great experience if you play it with friends. The problems I have with the multiplayer are problems that can be seen in singleplayer as well. Firstly, the population cap of 200 is too small. Secondly, the path finding is at times utterly horrendous. Thirdly stone and gold are too rare on big maps. You also need to keep in mind that this game has no scout button for your scout, you have to scout manually, and no "aggressive movement/attack move button". And last but not least comes a problem that is pretty much a problem with Age of Empires 2 in general. The units and buildings are not diverse enough. Races differ from each other only a little bit and thus you have the same units on each side which is incredibly boring in my eyes.
3. Graphics: The Graphics are absolutely okay. You can not expect a lot from such an old game. Fact is, Age of Empires 2 HD looks old enough to give you the feeling you had in the past, it reminds you strongly of the old Age of Empires 2, yet it is also modern and pretty enough to make it playable.
4. Sound: The sound effects as well as the music in this game are epic. They are not necessarily good but simply so iconic and well known that they can be considered classic and thus good.
5. Price: 20 € is too much for this game, but you can catch it for 10 in pretty much every sale.
6. Summary and score: It's an old classic. It has problems that may exist forever but it is playable and definitely fun. My recommendation is to buy it with a few friends in a sale, save money, have fun and don't take it too seriously.

Proteus makes Dear Esther look like GTAV.
I know sometimes developers read these reviews, and I don't like to be cruel. So please forgive me, devs, if you read this.
Proteus is a horrible piece of pretentious garbage. It was given to me as a gift, so I gave it a try. After 20 minutes I am totally and completely finished, and I have absolutely no idea what I am meant to get out of this.
Proteus is about wandering a pastel day-glo island where NOTHING HAPPENS. You can walk into obelisks (oh boy) and you'll get teleported to other parts of the island. Sometimes animals will scurry out of your way. Once in a while glowing lights will form into a circle and you can stand in it, and then it goes from night to day. Hold on to your hats, people!
Maybe I'm missing something. Maybe I'm not appreciating the subtle, inexorable beauty of this minimalist enterprise. Maybe I'm bringing faulty hard-hearted expectations from console shoot-em-ups into something which is clearly trying to tread a different path, one of intangible essences and abstract textures. Maybe I'm going to puke all over my keyboard.
While I appreciate everyone who tries something different, that does not automatically qualify their products for a badge of quality, fun, or beauty. In this case I have experienced none of those. Just a boring romp around a boring island.
I feel like 20 precious minutes of my life have been wasted, and I want them back. Stay away!

Right now, this game is not even a dollar. For that price, I'm not expecting the level of art and creativity found here. For that, I have to commend it. However, with indie games/cheap games, there are often trade offs. You want a brilliant story? The gameplay might be weak. You want a great story and good gameplay? The graphics might be terrible.
So what's this game's trade off? Unfortunately, it's usability. The game is ***CUMBERSOME***
I'll briefly go down a list of pros, I'll be a bit more in-depth for the cons, then my closing thoughts.
Pros:
-Cheap
-Easy to get into
-Content
--Plenty of levels, heroes, loot, etc. to utilize, for the cheap price you're getting a lot
-Co-op
-No port forwarding nonsense needed
-Relatively active community/devs
Cons:
-Stuttering
--For such a simple game, I should not be stuttering so consistently. It's most often with a couple of enemies around, but sometimes it's just with a boss. It's quite ridiculous, really. This game should run 900 frames a second on a decent machine (which I have). I can understand with hoards upon hoards of enemies with explosions and other effects going on, but sometimes it's just a couple of rats
-Buggy
--The few bugs I've run into; invulnerable enemies that require my blood to be killable (if this is part of the game, something on screen would help, but one rat dies, its brother takes no damage, a little confusing). I've crashed twice trying to navigate the menus. I tried to lower the master volume, and the bar shot across the screen passed where I could actually click it. And yes, it raised the sound 500%. I had to start the game to get the master volume bar to be visible
-UI
--The game requires WASD or other key inputs to navigate. That's a big no no on PC games. Please make it so the mouse clicks are read on menu screens. You want to see how your helm compares to the new ones you looted? Well, wasd to get to the helmet. Then push F to compare your helmet to helmets in your inventory. Then wasd up and down the helmets you own, pushing F on each and every one because you can't actually see stats until you equip the item. Push G to get out of the helmets and check your chest pieces, weapons, whatever. Can get very confusing with multiple items of each, and it's not fast in the slightest which it sorta needs to be in this game. That's just an example though, I really do not like the UI in this game.
-Four directional limited attacks
--Seriously why can't I shoot diagonally?
-Melee seems incredibly unbalanced compared to the ranged heroes
--Bosses sometimes will one hit you on contact. Good luck being a melee character then. (THIS COULD BE DUE TO ME SUCKING AT THE GAME/NOT GETTING VERY FAR YET)
A lot of cons, a lot of pretty damning cons. However, the game is fun. I don't know what it is about it, perhaps it's how satisfying it is to go from shooting 30 damage arrows, to shooting 300, to shooting 3000. The satisfaction is real. I would easily recommend this game without the long list of cons. I still recommend it, I do have to warn any pondering buyers; this game is flawed. You're not exactly paying a lot so you can't expect a golden goose, but it's still worth mentioning.
If you have even 1 friend that wants to join, get this game. If you have more, it's a blast. Even with the stuttering, unbearable UI, and annoying lack of diagonal combat.

Then there's the AI. Okay so, being that I couldn't play quests with players means I have to resort to AI partners. Which brings me to my next point which is that the enemy AI and programming is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T. I swear the developers hate us because they programmed the cheapest, most ♥♥♥♥ed up AI combat scenarios ever. Some enemies have god armor, and cannot be staggered by hits. In addition they may have infinite Ki/stamina and spam the same attack over and over and over. I feel like if I can fight and kill Beerus in a 1v1, then how the ♥♥♥♥ can Android 17 and 18 beat my♥♥♥♥♥so bad? Or why the hell are all the super saiyans non staggered and infinite Ki? Jesus I can only take Super Kamehameha so many times throughout a match without throwing my controller.
And then there's the story.
So I just beat the game right, and may I say it was a seriously ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t story you go through. Sure I'm fine with ripping off Time Cop and helping the DBZ universe get fixed, but it seems like they put so much emphasis into the damn Saiyan and Frieza sagas and then just said, "♥♥♥♥ it! This game is getting too damn long!" Once I beat Frieza and *SPOILER ALERT*
I was already fighting Cell and I was like, "Wait a minute.....they skipped some♥♥♥♥♥♥" And it didn't stop there. Immediately I found after the Cell Saga I beat the Buu saga in what was like the blink of an eye and then there was the end of the game. I could go on to ♥♥♥♥♥ about things like how the RNG is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, and how the framerate and tearing and graphics are crap, but you get the idea.

The solo/offline is great, there is no lag and the game is enjoyable to play through the story and pq quests. Online is the exact opposite, it seems online sessions are hosted peer-to-peer or something equally horrible. This is a fighting game and you need to land those combos at exactly the right time and this is almost impossible while playing online. For example most grab moves/strikes you cannot land, most of the time you will see you character thrust out his hand to grab and it will actually slightly push away the enemy and the grab just does not happen, like WTF annoying.
I live in Canada with a 3MB/s and 1MB/s up and whenever i try to search for only online matches in my region there is no results, ever. The server browser when looking for a match takes around 15 seconds to complete, then you look through the list and click on a match and it takes another 15 seconds to 'connect' and half the time the lobby is full and you have basically wasted a minute. Every time this happens you have to refresh the entire list as it kicks you out of the entire menu. This in itself doesn't seem like a lot of time but take into account the fact the PQ's only take 5 -10 minutes then after it completes you have to run all the way back to the online desk to look for match and then wait to an absurd amount of time.
Sometimes when you join a lobby and the host has medium connection 'bars' on his connection status I think: ok not a bad connection the PQ/lag will probably be alright. What usually happens is the game loads and everyone is standing around then after a few seconds people will move slightly and look like they are in motion/flying but they are not moving at all. By the way you cannot leave an online match unless you alt+f4. In the case i listed above enemies will die before you even get to them or if you do they will teleport around the map becuase the lag is so bad you cannot even hit them even while next to them, their hp will not move. I have not had such a horrible online experience, ever.
Please look past my non proofread grammar mistakes and hear what I am saying, my connection is great i can play BF3, TF2, FFXI/FFXIV and a slather of other online games without lag but I am left with the feeling that without a dedicated group/friends to play with (with good connections and even then... sometimes it doesn't matter) the online experience is absolutely despicable, gdi this game could have been great.

This is an user friendly game review/in game useer manual for Interstellar marines xDDDDD
Interstellar Marines, is an first person shooter game (FPS)
It is yet only in the early-access stage wich means that this game may, or may not be finished. But as it seems like right now the devs will continue this game. The first impression of this game when i first saw the video that plays when you first start up the game was great. the game has great overall graphics and suits pretty much all computers (within limitations) you do not need to have an super computer to play this game and it gives good fps.
In the begining you will start straight on the training course to get used to the controls.
then you are on your'e own. you can choose to play either single player (story mode/campaign) or you can jump over to co-op or versus mode. but first off im gonna talk about single player:
Single player means that you play versus the computer, (also called bots/Ai's)
The bots in this game are well made, they seem to be "artificial intelligent" they detect you easier when you stand/run than they do when you crouch and move slowly.
In game you will also have the options to equip lights (F), laser aim on your gun (G) or supressor (Q) when you use laser and the flashlight in game be carefull,\ because other players in game can see the laser and the flashlight (bots too)
they detect you a lot more faster when you have laser and flashlight enabled.
If you do not use the sound supressor on your gun, then be adviced. within a few seconds you will hear tons of robots stomping in the ground and coming sprinting towards you and ready to bash your skull in with their fists :)
the envoirment in the game is mostly dark/foggy so it is hard to spot enemies as well as it is hard to stay hidden if you will have to use your flashlight. this is why i often like strobing the flashlight for few moments as it can be mistaken to be lights in game that flimmers.
The thing with this game is that there are not very many guns. wich makes this game more focused on how actually skilled you are isntead of all the gear.
some peopels like it. some peoples dont.
the physics in the game are great. movement are well balanced as well as the gravity, in this game you do not have a bar that shows your stamina. but you still have it. so dont be sprinting around like a maniac. because this will affect how well you can aim when youre standing still as you will soon start to breathe like you have held your breath for 5 mina haha.
in game you can comunicate with different players. both with text and with voice chat. voice (V) chat is more prefered as the text does not show up before you open the "text menu" where you writes your messages, so they do not pop up on your screen automatically.
If you like to change graphics settings or general game settings and key bindings, then there is an fair ammount of options to use. and the game has a good compability to most screens. wich is quite good as i am using an 50" tv while i play. wich can be troubling in many games.
Also, every single bullet you fire in this game counts. the STATS menu will show you absolutely everything, and by saying this i mean absolutely EVERYTHING
you can see how many bullets you have shot, how many kills, how many deaths, kill/death ratio, wich body part you have hit the most. and how many times you have hit the different body parts counted per bullet.
so theres lot of room for competition with your friends about the best stats.
it is also displaying what your favourite weapon is.
The in game controls are easy to maneuver and is easy to get used to.
If you want to play online either in co-op or in versus battles there are plenty of servers in different locations so you can use the filters to browse for servers that is filling your recuirements of ping, difficulty, game mode and so on.
If you have any questions or any issues or maby even a bug report then you can just contact the devs via twitter, facebook or the steam game forum page, they are really fast at responding. and they are also really friendly.
i have already reported in a few bugs that aint a big deal and they responded within 20 minutes.
GG DEVS AND KEEP IT UP!
so i give the support area an 10/10 points just for that.
One of the biggest thigns about this game is that even it is a futuristic/sci-fi game it is still really realistic wich means things work out in the game as it would in real life, as an example: laser aim. in many games they make the laser beams a solid red beam that is highly visiblie to all players. but i real life you would not be able to see the laser beam unless theres some dust particles in the air. the more dust particles in the air, the more visiblie the beam gets.
and in the game. it is just slightly visiblie as it is under normal circumstances in real life.
the flashlight is dynamic light. it fades over distance and lights up the room like a real flashlight. it is not a static/flat light.
BEAUTIFUL!
when you run, your character starts breathing more heavily. and starts to run slower.
if you get injured. your vision will become blurry and you will have an hard time to see your surroundings until you recover.
in the interview of the devs they say they wanted to create this game as realistic as possiblie for sci-fi games. and they did it pretty well!
in general this game is a whole lot of fun and really exciting and it is a great game and personally i have high expectations for this game as it got such big potentional to become something big and if you like fps games. then this is the game for you.

As a starting player, this game would appear to have some serious issues with balance. Starting out you have pea shooters and bare-bones for armour. You learn the basics mostly against bots, and the rare other sub-1000 player. Takes about 10 seconds to join a game. Fair enough. I progress to level 2, 3, 4, no issues. Still not enough scrap to craft another MG but as I level I get a few new parts and finally a couple extra MGs as rewards, so I mount those in place of the starters. Power score is now 1200. Go to join a new game, gonna try the Shotgun match... No joy. Sit there for over 2 minutes, no game. Switch from Australia to Asia to give it a go.. 40 seconds and I get into a game of mostly real players... Cool. Except it's not cool. Power ratings range from ~1200 ~ 1500, seems fair enough, except several of the vehicles are running cannon builds?!
A system of power ratings is fine, but when you're stacked into games where you don't even remotely have access to the same types of equipment as other players? Maybe these are "glass cannon" builds, but when you don't even have the parts to set up redundant wheels, one hit from a 57mm effectively cripples whatever a starting player can hope to field.
Dunno, I was expecting to get my♥♥♥♥♥handed to me by seal clubbers with more experience, both in terms of build options and map knowledge, but running into stuff like that is a bit of a crap experience. Coming from War Thunder the progression of firepower is fairly linear where clubbers are free to enter the arena with the seals, but it is with the same equipment. The edge being experienced crews and their own personal experience. I mean no one can slap 37mm cannon pods on a biplane for giggles because they happen to have one in their storage.
Seems like a fun game, but combining a starting grind like that and getting stacked into games with completely lopsided options for armaments and equipment as well as in-game experience, I can't see that growing a player base.
*Update: This initial experience was a bit disappointing, but I believe is was due more to the region and time of day more than anything, with a low player count bumping me into higher than normal PS battles on the night. Matches on following days looked to be more balanced in terms of equipment on the field. One other thing worth noting is that the initial introduction to the game does not cover off the Marketplace. Selling things like crates gives you enough coin to buy things like extra wheels to help ensure that you aren't crippled on the first unlucky cannon hit. (can easily afford a cannon as well, or shotguns to experiment and learn with rather than waiting on the level progression.) My negative assessment is not about the game balance (which will likely continue to be adjusted) more about the experience of a new player in the game, relative to experiences with other MMO games as a new player. As a new player, the impression you get is that certain equipment is "locked" until you get to a certain level, but then to get put in the field against that equipment it is a highly discouraging experience. The equipment itself is not locked, just the ability to craft it. Crafting white parts is pretty much completely pointless as the scrap can be sold for considerably more than the price of the parts.

I'll start by saying that my only real prior experience of this series comes from the first game which I played on PS3 and very much enjoyed. That said I can't comment on how true it remains to the story in the manga or anime or whatever. Yet, it delivers a stunning movie like experience that rivals that of games like Metal Gear Solid and the Yakuza series. The attention to graphical detail is top notch and I've encountered very very few graphical errors which is pretty impressive for a console port. Going back to the cinemographic experience, the game is locked at 30 FPS in order to maintain the feel of the anime and even so it plays really smooth.
The gameplay itself is more reminiscent of a button mashy beat-em-up or more like one of the Dragon Ball Z fighting games than a true fighter. However, there is definitely a little bit of skill involved in managing your chakra and substitutions in on-line battles. Right now the on-line seems hit or miss. Some people can't connect to me at all, however with one person I played 10 matches without a single error and no major latency issues. Hopefully a patch will be deployed to fix the on-line issues. Single player vs cpu versus is available in addition to a local 2 player versus. The single player story mode starts off exciting, hits some slow points, then gets pretty good again and held my attention.
Overall, as someone who is not a typical fan of the series I can highly reccomend this game to anyone who wants to enjoy something not typically found on PC. It is easily one of the best looking games I've played in a while.

This game does a lot right, and little wrong. Servers are privately hosted, just like how classic Star Wars: Battlefront 2 was. 90% of the time people respect the server rules. 90% of the time you'll have a squad that works together, communicates well, and helps people learn the game. Run into a toxic player? Just swap squads or swap teams. Don't ever let one bad apple ruin this game for you, there's only one out of three dozens in my experience. They never last long, either. Contact a sever admin and they'll generaly remove toxicity from their server for obvious reasons.
Combat is not a traditional lobby-shooter. You do not roam around at max speed and then shoot without aiming. Hip-fire is do-able but very inaccurate. You need to iron-sight aim for proper accuracy. Work as a team, or die alone. You'll find the longer respawns compared to other games a harsh lesson for going lone-wolf and not supporting your squad.
Patience is key, reliablity is a virture. You need to embody both for proper success in this. Your squad needs to be able to request you do something, and know you're performing said role/function without deviation. A marksman on overwatch should not be sneaking behind enemy lines to rack kills, nor should a medic be charging in Rambo style.
This game is a great match for people who want a game that looks at 'realism', adds in what is fun and cuts away what doesn't work, focusing more on game mechanics being fun than full-on realism. This isn't a one man carries the whole team kind of shooter. You can go with zero kills, a few deaths, and still have done a great job for the team. There's more than just straight out shooting and killing, with various support roles.

Plush is a ragdoll physics game set in a small girl's room at bedtime. She can't sleep unless all her plush toys are arranged on her bed in exactly the way they prefer, and each of them have their own picky preferences. The goal is to move the toys around the bed and place them according to their preferences, taking care not to knock any of them on the floor and lose the round. There's a little bit more nuance to it, but that's basically the overall gist of the 40 stages this game contains.
I played through the first tutorial stages on Normal difficulty then restarted on Hard once I got the idea, taking about an hour to complete every challenge. There's an additional Play Room mode available from the very start that allows you to place any number of any toy you want on the bed (limited only by the power of your computer) and see what happens, but it's pretty much just a physics demo with little else to really do beside some mildly amusing chaos. And that's all the content there is for the game.
It's presented in a nice enough way with adequate visuals and some really nice, relaxing music, and the little girl's voice-over is adorable. The narrator/father(?) isn't quite so lovable, though, and sounds a little gruff and not exactly what you'd immediately imagine being the soothing voice for a bedtime story. I'm guessing the voice work was done by the developer and his daughter? If that is the case then it makes sense and I guess adds a certain charm to it. But if they were outside help hired for the job then it seems an odd choice.
The biggest complaint I have about this game, though, is the controls. It's done entirely with the mouse as you click on a toy and drag it around, but there's a huge disconnect between cursor and toy, and often you'll find the former getting far ahead of the latter as you try to drag a plush around, get it jammed in something, then struggle as it either fails to respond at all, or else suddenly flies off wildly and causes you to drop it and lose the round. You can essentially take any notion of precision you have and check it in at the door, coz you won't be needing it for this game.
As hugely irritating as that was, I did still love the basic premise and breezed through it quickly enough to not stay too mad at it. Although I feel the price is a little steep for what it is and couldn't recommend it for any more than half the current €4 asking price. More content or modes would have been nice, but if you have the patience for the controls and want some cute little puzzles to solve, this is worth trying out.
