Cute rag-doll physics puzzle game.
I expect somebody thought "my kids don't play with dolls" and instead made a game based on "rag animal physics". You have 40 puzzles where teddy bears need to snuggle up to each other, cats jump away if you move something next to them (and hippos make everyone jump away), "Mr Stinkypants" who needs to be kept away from everyone else, unmovable pillow obstacles that you're not allowed to cross, and in two of the three difficulty levels, the floor is lava. It took me ~4 hours to do and re-do each of the 40 puzzles on each difficulty level to get the achievements.
These 40 puzzles would actually be suitable for small children, but the rag doll physics are not. It is never clear where you're grabbing the animal that you're moving, it seems to be attached to the pointer by a weak spring that elongates itself, which means accurate placement is nearly impossible, and sometimes you can grab animals mid-air and sometimes you can't. This lack of precision means that most of the time I've been fighting the physics instead of solving the puzzle. (And why don't I get the achievement for completing all levels on normal when I completed them on hard?) Sure, the children's voices are a nice touch, but I don't really know to whom I could recommend this game. Well, here goes:
If you like to fiddle with ragdoll physics, and if you like stuffed animals and childrens' voices, this is the game you've been waiting for. If you don't, it's probably not.

When I first got this game I was really skeptical towards it. I'm glad that I gave it a try, because I was totally wrong.
Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is a kart racing game with tons of characters and stages. Something that I love about it is that, unlike other kart games, characters aren't limited to the main franchise (Sonic, in this case). There are
You'll be able to play with characters coming from games such as Space Channel 5, NiGHTS into Dreams, Jet Set Radio, Crazy Taxi, etc. Steam version includes unlikely characters from games like Team Fortress 2, Football Manager and even from other media like the movie Wreck-It Ralph and real life racer Danica Patrick, or youtuber Yogscast. Counting with DLC, S&ASRT includes 7 characters from the Sonic franchise, out of 31 playable characters (for comparison, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe has 36 Mario characters out of 42), showing the diversity of the game. For guys like me that aren't too fond of Sonic, this is amazing, since it has characters for all sorts of tastes.
, and like the characters they come from different Sega franchises. In addition to this variety, there are changes within the stages themselves that make the gameplay more dinamic. All stages have 3 laps, and it's uncommon that the level stays the same between all laps: parts of the roads are destroyed, streets make way to water sections, a ramp propels your kart into turning into a plane, etc. The levels are fun to play, and include different routes for you to explore and try to outrace your rivals.
The story mode is made not only of races, it also has other stages that help you learning and improving different skills that are useful for racing, including how to best use boosting, drifting, items, etc. You learn by directed action and practicing, not by boring lengthy tutorials. This lack of hand helding is very good, but at the same time the game doesn't leave you alone, it provides the tools to improve. This evolution will prove itself useful, since
. Nothing better than the rewarding feeling you get after you finally beat that frustrating stage on a hard difficulty.
Along with the single player story mode,
(either with your friends or random matches with people from all over the world),
Although there a few achievements that depend on multiplayer (both online and local), the focus of the game is on its story mode. On story mode, each level completed awards you from 1 to 4 stars, depending on the difficulty you completed it, encouraging you to replay them on higher difficulties. These stars are the currency you use to go further into the story mode, as well as unlocking new characters. You can also unlock "mods", basically options to customize your racer's stats, like speed or acceleration. Unfortunately there are no further customization options like in other racing games, like changing your kart or changing character colors. There are three DLCs, that add three characters and one stage, but even without them the game has plenty of playtime before you can unlock everything on the base game.
Graphics are good for a racing game. You can't expect groundbreaking aesthetics, but
. The models have that kind of quality in which, even though they're not realistic, they look nice, and for me that's all that matters. I should add that the game is well optimized, my computer is far from being among the best ones out there, but in all my time playing this I never had performance issues. Likewise, the soundtrack probably won't get you amazed by its beauty, but it's energetic and unobstrusive - all that a racing game soundtrack needs to be.

Piranha Bytes' games have never been about mindless slaughter, but rather deep and careful exploration of the rich environment, carefully crafted quests, interesting characters and total immersion. Risen 2 may have strayed away a bit from some of these factors, but I can confidently say that Risen 3 has certainly improved greatly over it, and the feeling and atmosphere of the game is much more reminiscent of the original Gothic games and the first Risen.
One of the biggest complaints of the previous game in the Risen series was the combat system. This time, however, not only is the magic system back, adding greater variety, but melee combat feels much more satisfying, and it's certainly NOT a left click fest - if you want to defeat a strong enemy, you must dodge, block, riposte and time your hits.
Risen 3: Titan Lords is a game for all the players who loved Piranha Bytes' classical works. Perhaps the plot isn't up to par with Gothic 1's, but nevertheless, as the final game in the series, it has certainly lived up to its promise to go back to the roots - the more observant fans will even notice some very pleasant surprises involving familiar characters from times gone by.

The controls need work though, I found the controls when fighting to be a little clunky but damn if that Dark Souls type dodge roll button didn't save my a$$ several times when I got caught up in an ambush. I was spamming that button like mad. And there was a nice bit of satisfaction when in a sword fight and finishing off the threat by blasting it with my pistol.
Oh and speaking of finishing off. I like that sometimes you will see a finishing animation after a fight. It's not shown often like in other games where you get tired of seeing the same finishing animations over and over, but you will see them here and there and it mixes up pretty well by offering different types of finishing animations and camera views like when ramming your sword in a guys stomach or catching him from behind in a struggle to cut his neck open with your sword for example. I thought I was dead for sure, Dark Souls dodge rolling all over the place for my life. Next thing I see the NPC running to save my a$$ and he casts a heal spell on me almost immediately and starts kicking the sh!# out the threat. I was like O.O
One more thing I have to mention. Even though the voice acting is... terrible, you will laugh at the dialogue. There is some serious humor and cursing in this game. LOL. Try wandering off in the beginning and your sister will ask you. "Hey, where you going? Do you even know what your doing? Are you Fu#%ing lost?" And you can choose to hide behind your pride and answer back, "No I'm not Fu#%ing lost! I know exactly what I'm doing!" Knowing damn well you don't. xD
Anyway, I can say I am happy with this game. It is fun and very satisfying. :)

This is truly a sleeper hit - I got it as part of some sonic sale combo quite some time ago and it has been a regular contender for casual gameplay since! The gameplay is intuitive, and there is a very respectable difficulty curve that really tasks you with learning the minutae of the game mechanics (drifitng, boosting and the typical Kart weaponry).  The campaign is an unusually long-lasting affair without being overly repetitive, and the options for local, single and online grand-prix/mirror and custom racing is a real draw for (as of time of this post) a still very vibrant online community.
Easily and highly recommended.

This game is a lot like other Lego games. It's a mad romp through your favorite world, and it's a lot of fun. I really enjoyed it. But, it's not quite as good as Lego Starwars III, or Lego The Hobbit.
The normal Lego game system is pretty easy to grasp. You can play through the story, where you play as the characters who were there in the book or movie, and then, at the end, unlock the ability to play as them in other missions, and use their special abilities to unlock secrets. Lego: The Lord Of The Rings does this very well, with the Mithril Bricks, Minikits, True Adventurer, etc. The missions are loads of fun, with puzzles that are a tad glitchy, to those that are well designed, but hard!
So, the reason that this game is not as good as some of the others from Lego, is that it's just not quite as... I'm not sure. But my other two Lego games, which I mentioned above, have a pizzaz that Lego:TLOTR just doesn't have. It's still a great game (although, if you play without a controller, finding your way around middle earth is an absolute nightmare, because the camera angle is never where you want it), and I heartily recommend it. But only if you've played through the other games first, and want some more.

Gameplay:
- Really stable PvE gameplay

- Haven't really seen, but think you can make your own "what-if" battles
Character Creation:
- Enough customizations to get a feel of what your ideal DBZ character should be

- 3 Battle Types ( In terms of stats they don't affect it, just the move sets given)
PvE:

I've only played this game for 6 hours as of now, but I've gotten to rank 25 online, which isn't too bad considering 80% of people who're on there are all under rank 8.
The gameplay is surprisily very good. Realistic, and yet not too hard.  The guns will move a bit upwards if you hold the trigger, but is still controllable, and confortable, so it's not bad. Just like other good FPS games like Battlefield(s), Medal of Honor, etc. The scope on your assault rifle is 4x zoom, but only has 20, contrary to your main weapon, which is a SMG, and holds 30. Nevertheless, the assault rifle packs a big punch, and if used right, can prove useful as a sniper would. Very accurate and easy to use. The SMG however, is all a SMG is really; quick firing, red dot scope, light, 30 round clip. Overall I like them both for what they are; one is close range, the other long range.
So I haven't done very many of the single player missons yet, but I've played all the online maps that there are, which is 9. All of them are fun in their own way. The winter one is very *cough*cool*cough*, the swamp map is a nightmere in the dark, but still freakily fun, and the others are well-made with lots of spots to hide behide, and lots of spots to round a corner and get shot in the face, or walk up to a building in the dark only to find out a guy is in the shadows *dead*. Overall, they're great maps in a sci-fi setting. You won't get bored of them very quickly.
The laser on the guns is awesome. You can see the point of it no matter where it is shining. (in the tree, on the ground, or 4 miles away) The only con about it is, in most maps whether in the dark, or rain, snow, etc, you can see the whole beam of light. Which makes it very easy to find the man holding the gun.
The flashlight is very bright, but gives you away in a *cough*flash*cough*. You have to pick the right moments to turn it on. if you're in a big room, and you think you saw someone, it's totally worth turning it on to get a kill. or at least see where you are in the pitch-black moments.
The silencer works, and I haven't noticed any reduced velocity as of yet.
You have unlimited ammo. Keep reloading till your R button is broken. I litterally reload even if I only used two bullets. A good habit to have.
Overall the gadgets have their advantages and disadvantages. Once you start playing you figue out what works best for you.

Although the two guns they give you by default are amazing, they do get old after awhile. And so far the game only has the two. I'm sure the devlopers will add more as they continue to add things to the game, but for now you'll have to live with the only two.

Oh yes, everyone's worst nightmere! Well, unlike other games that don't have team tags above players, this one does. The problem is once you get shot to a degree, your whole hub in your face screen shuts down for about 10 - 15 seconds.  In that time the person who shot you could be right outside the doorway, but the only way you can tell if it's him or your teammate is if you see a little blue on him, (which is hard to see anyways) as the friendly tags and all the digital things you see in the game are gone. (except your sites on the guns)  So yeah, there is a fair share of team killing, but it also makes it interesting for yourself when you get shoot.
Yes, when you die in an online match, (not co-op, I don't know what it's like for co-op) it takes about 100 - 120 seconds to respawn in a ten minute game. And you only have 15 seconds to be revived, which isn't very much at all, seeing is how you have to be careful in this game. I enjoy this game's visual aesthetic, and its sound effects are nice. I also like the towers themselves, for the most part. However, I don't think I've ever played a more stressful tower defense game in my life. Keep in mind that I love Sanctum 2, and it has you running all over the place and shooting at enemies while you're getting attacked, and alternating primary and secondary fire and different guns, worrying about reloading fast enough to kill enemies before they reach the core, etc. With PixelJunk Monsters, however, if you take even a second to try to strategize mid-game, you're probably already screwed. How so? Well, let's see...
The mobs of enemies come in a few seconds after the map loads. You do not have time to look at it and decide where to put a tower. In fact, there are typically multiple spawn points on every map, and the game never tells you which point the next wave will be spawning from until they're already there, and by then, it's probably too late for you to build a tower that will be sufficient. While I'm reeling from seeing which side the enemy is already barreling down and I'm trying to play damage control to just barely stop them in time, the next wave is about to spawn, and by the time I finish dealing with the first wave, the second wave has already spawned. Which side(s) do they spawn on? Good luck guessing. Choose poorly and you're going to lose some lives. Building from the end outward will help, but only so much, due to the range and firing speeds of the towers.
Well, at least you can just sit back and spend money like crazy, building towers fast and succeed, right? Haha, no. The whole time your towers are killing, you control a little Tiki guy who you have to run around to pick up coins the enemies drop. Don't go fast enough? The coins disappear, meaning you are permanently handicapped on that run in terms of how much you have to spend on towers. Gem stones also drop on occasion, and if you don't pick those up, you could miss them, too.
Gem stones are used to unlock the superior towers a few minutes into each match, and not only do you have to make sure you grab them when enemies drop them, but there are also two trees in a literal small forest on every map which will pop out a gem stone each. If you don't find these, chances are you will be delayed in getting the superior towers, which will likely lead to more lives lost, because the inferior towers are worthless against certain enemies.
On that note, enemies will spawn with a glow to them; a certain color. They might be green, blue, red, or not glow at all. The game doesn't tell you what this means. Each glow typically means the enemy is weak to a certain "element" from your towers. It's nothing super obvious and clear cut. You will need to either resort to trial and error, or look up a walkthrough to figure out what towers you need. If you don't get the right tower(s), chances are you're about to game over. All of the elemental towers are locked and require gem stones to unlock, so no, you can't just build one of everything to protect yourself, either, because you likely won't have enough gemstones to unlock more than one or two types of towers by the time these enemies pop up.
Well, if you just keep wildly running around like mad, at
you can get into the groove of that quick motion and keep things happening, right? Pffft, no. The game also expects you to either stand next to a tower,
doing the many other vital tasks, while waiting for a slowly-filling bar to fill up as your character dryly dances beside the tower to increase its stats. I could spend gem stones to level a tower faster, but then I don't have enough gem stones to unlock an elemental tower and the glowing enemies waltz by my non-elemental towers and give me a game over.
So let's recap! The game wants you to run around searching trees for gem stones
setting up towers and having to physically have your character next to the build site to place them,
knowing where to build which towers despite having no clue which of the multiple entrances the enemies will come from,
collecting the coins and gem stones they drop,
dancing next to towers to level them up very slowly,
watching for the element(s) to unlock to deal with whatever color glow the enemies show up with. So much being demanded of the player simultaneously and immediately removes the ability to strategize, which, in my opinion, is one of the vital elements of a tower defense, instead calling for rapid, sloppy actions and an inability to ever feel satisfied with watching my towers kill enemies, because I'm overloaded with busy work the second the game starts.
Like I said, Sanctum 2 is an exciting TD/FPS hybrid, and I loved it. Back in highschool, I thought "eustress" was a stupid vocabulary word. Who ever heard of "good stress?" No stress at all is better, or so I thought. Then I began looking deeper into things, and it finally clicked that there is such a thing as good stress. Having something to do every day, even if it isn't necessarily "fun," that gets you out of bed is an important thing in life. You might have stressors, but all stress isn't bad. It can be good and makes life interesting and helps with honing skills and even getting better at a job to be ready for promotions or potentially managing, etc. However, if there is stress in your life that drives you to anger and frustration regularly, it's not eustress. It's just a thorn in your side that should be pulled out and discarded. PixelJunk Monsters has no qualities that can redeem it for me, as it drives me to anger without any positive fulfillment or satisfaction.

I really don't always want to be the first guy to downvote popular games, but honestly, in this state the physics and especially the collision system make this game an experience with way more frustration potential than it should have.
If it were priced $10, the very gimmicky nature of this title would probably mandate a negative review anyway.
At the very friendly $4 price point seen here, the lacking depth and optimisation (try throwing 100-200 plushies into the air at decent gfx settings!) certainly are
able, however to be classified moderately jolly, some improvements are needed.
That pillows are rigid bodies is a questionable design choice deeply ingrated into the design of many of the game levels, however it's very much immersion-breaking, and trying to shove a stuffed animal through a tight pillow funnel of unbendable durasteel is simply not fun. There's also the potential of them getting stuck inbetween pillows, as well as for animals to be on the floor in unreachable areas.
Victory conditions are glitchy (I've had levels end with tanks still on the bed, or with plushies moving in mid-air), and on hard mode, the fail condition comes with bugs like not resetting (but instead just suspending all animation) when an animal is on the night stand.
Plushies also have entirely different physics behaviour if you are controlling them versus if you are moving them by pushing them -- for example, a ginormous hippo is light like a feather if you just push it with something else, or a Scaredy Cat doesn't get nervous if it's pushed towards something that should set it off by another object. This might be by design for puzzle purposes, but like the pillow-rocks, it's not fun.
What is fun, however, are the nice voice-overs and the animal names (even if "MSP" should probably be a bit more colourful, like a pink/blue checkers pattern).
With a lot more polish, this could well turn into a positive review (extra bonus points for fluffy pillows!).

Proteus is the Skyrim of appreciation. Sometimes we forget that video games are an experience we pay for, like go-karting, drugs, etc. Proteus is something special. It gives you something you didn't even realize you needed. There is no plot, no dialogue, no quests, no lore, no fall damage, no achievements, no interacting with items - the closest thing to interaction is the spacebar has you lay down and walking near certain objects activates some things. You don't HAVE to do anything. Proteus is about you, your thoughts, and a very lovingly-created world that you never knew you had always wished existed. Have you ever had a dream you loved being in, and then woken up saddened that it wasn't real? Did you think afterward of the excitement it stirred in you to explore this new world? That is where this game takes it's bliss.
It's a world where everything has it's own voice. You awake in the water and make your way to an island. The trees in the forest sing in daylight and hum at night. You spot some chickens and chase them about the forest (incidentally, this is how the game began for me and I'm unashamed to say I was giggling the whole time). Wistful clouds appear on the purple horizen as the moon rises. Speck by speck you see the stars dot the sky, some unhinging from the starscape and meandering off in whatever direction pleases them most. Proteus is a world where you have no worries. The only thing to do is frolic. Don't worry, nobody is around to judge you. Nobody needs your help right now. It's okay to feel peace.
If any of what I've said resonated with you, buy Proteus and thank yourself. You've earned this.

This game is a gem and you wont find many others like it. It has so much heart and character. The world just feels so deliberately crafted. Everything in the game world is placed with a purpose. This design choice deviates from the random events and occurrences in modern games like Skyrim, but brings to the table a feeling that this world was crafted with care and attention to detail. This, among other things such as the loot, craftable materials, varied jungles, caves, beaches, fortresses and more make exploration a real treat! My favorite location is Calador, a volcanic island with a massive waterfront fortress and green bonfires dotting the coastline. It really is a sight to behold!
Ultimately, this game is all about getting lost in the vast world and forging your own destiny! It's about exploring and finding all of the secrets and content packed into the game! it's about side quests, and loot, and character progression, and choice! The choice to pick a direction, any direction, and be confident that there will be something new to discover right around the next corner. It's about all of these things... and while the game certainly isn't perfect, it's definitely a rare gem in a sea of mainstream rpgs that all try to do the same thing over and over.
In short, if you're a Gothic/Risen fan, you know what you're getting into, and this is some of PB's finest work. You may love it, you may hate it, but I urge anyone who's on the fence to give it a shot! I hope you can find as much enjoyment in this game as I have so far.

Put simply, Proteus is lovely.  It's very simple, and it's not a very long game (one could find everything it has to offer so far in one or two sittings), but it is very attractive and soothing.
There is no combat, no story, no progression in the strictest sense.  There is only exploration -- the game starts with the player out at sea just off a randomly-generated island.  The island itself is unpopulated, save for the local flora and fauna, but it is dotted with landmarks that must have been placed by people at some point (gravestones, towers, statues, etc.).  The origin of these objects is not the point, however.
The only progression comes in the form of a vortex that appears at night, which will move the player forward through time, bringing them into the next season.  The appearance of the island changes from season to season, as do the resident fauna.  Each season seems to have its own strange occurrences as well.  (Here's a tip: don't enter the vortex on the first night of summer.  Stick around for the second day.)
All in all, I highly recommend Proteus for anyone who enjoyed Flower or Journey, or just wants to take a break and enjoy chasing frogs, chickens, and fireflies around a colorful island for a little while.

Risen 3 is Finally out and is now being hit by reviews that are up and down. Let me talk about my experience and what this game's strong point and weak points. Read first before you point that dangerous thumb at me.
As a new protaganist to the series, you are the son of steelbeard and brother of Patty who both are on the way to crab island to discover treasure from a map only to run into the army of the underworld and have your soul taken. The only thing you can do is to try to redeem it by battling against the forces of darkness
Risen 3 is a good improvement over 2 in many ways, Fans of PB's  original risen will love it, those who hated/loved 2 will also be welcomed back to the pirate theme with new improvements, and those that are new to the series will be a hit or miss. The game isn't like your typical rpg or Skyrim. It is a third person rpg with different style, rules and combat. Don't be mislead though this game isn't about sailing the open oceans or exploring a massive world but instead lets you explore certain lands of reasonable size that is filled with plenty of quests, dangers, and treasures.
The combat system itself feels more smooth this time around as as it reverts itself away from risen 2 and taps back to its root like Risen with some added tweaks and with a much more fun magic gameplay. Yes you do start this game off weak, in fact you'll have to depend on your companions which you can choose to bring one at a time during the game to help you. You'll have to count on them because enemies will swipe you, attack you from sides, dodge your attacks and even blind side you when you aren't looking and in groups. In fact hard mode can be quite a challenge during the start  game.
As you progress the game leveling the way you want you'll start realizing that your efforts will start paying off. You'll start investing in new skills to aid you in becoming stronger  even experiencing better combat which should feel a bit more fluid and much like original risen. You'll also  be able to switch weapons and spells via the bottom hotbars, while combining the use of  items and scrolls becoming more powerful in fact too powerful to the point where you're completely ridiculously almost overpowered, killing enemies in a few hits..
The game offers you a choice to join between 3 factions. Voodoo, Demon hunters, or Guardians and you can only commit to one so choose carefully. Each offering its own unique skills and spells to help you fight. Some though are similar to other faction.
The game leveling systems revolves around glory and gold. You earn glory from mostly killing and questing.The quest system in this game is well done in a way so that if you've already encountered the quest you'll be able to turn it in to the npc when it is requested eliminating that need to go back and forth. There are Plenty of quests and things to do in the game to acquire glory and gold.
The return of magic this time around is more  fun to play with depending on your faction you've picked.You'll be able to utilize spells from that faction otherwise you'll have to buy runes and scrolls.
Spells are also a completely seperate tree  and requires certain gems to purchase. When you attain spells you'll only be limited to casting by a cooldown timers. For every faction is a spell you can use as a melee spell over and over again.,You can even improve the timer and combo off more or cast faster. Yes I became a mage and I kick ♥♥♥ with a epee in my hand raining fireballs upon my enemies and stealing stuff by just reaching out my hands and did fire bending somagic this time around is  more fun.
Aside from the gameplay the sound and music is perfectly fine for this game, the graphics though a bit outdated is much better than its previous series for sure and the game feels more optimized (save for the 8 cores + situation). If you are a fan of the series you will see that it is NOT THAT BAD though could be improved much more. The voice acting is decent for  in the game  though  some are  a bit cheesy (such as bone) or bad but can be looked over because the dialogues actually get a bit better later in the game.. Sometimes you can see the devs joking around with the dialogue by adding really funny questions and phrases and isn't meant to be taken too seriously.
The quests themselves in this game contain many lore behind the world of risen 3 and will keep you wanting to do the quest. You'll have retrieval quests, kill quests, subquests, and mainquests. Not all quests are grindy at all or without purpose.
There are choice dialogues in this game and the choices affects the outcome of what happens. The choice is really up to you on how you want to play the game, maybe you'll steal, maybe you'll use your tongue and intimidate or pick another choice to accomplish your mission. maybe you rather be the bad guy and lose a bit of your humanity or gain humanity. Whatever you  choose to do in the game will either acquire your soul back or help you lose it much quicker.
anyways check the game out. This game might not be the cup of tea for everyone.
Make your own damn decision on the game. Don't be mislead  by naysayers and research it well.  I beaten the game around 25 hours and thats not doing EVERY quest there is in the game, once I became OP i went straight for the last mission. Reason is because I can save my other quests on the other islands for other playthroughs as different faction. I enjoyed the game quite a bit and hope that in the future they can improve on some of the cons I've written about the game.
+ Game starts off really slow  and difficult but gets better as you progress
+ Tons of quests, plenty of glory and gold to be found
+ Ship battle with sea monsters are challenging
+ The combat is much better than risen 2 but can feel a bit clunky at first until you progress a bit.
+ Quests systems completes if you done it already in the world so you don't have to actually grab it to do it you can turn it in as long as you've done it.
+ Magic is fun, try guardians and firebend.
+ You can be any class you want to be varying from 3 factions.
+ Plenty of gear to play around with and stats you can mix and match to your advantage. Legendary weapons included and upgraded weapons.
+- Reused map and game materials from 2
+- Subpar dialogue and lots of comedy and jokes, sometimes funny, sometimes cheesy, sometimes very bad
+- Some people will probabaly not like the way the combat is done, you get a certain amount of combo hit and you must dodge or attack your enemy.
- Armor feels more asthetic than useful sometimes, I found myself wearing adventurer armor during the entire game and barely changing to the other armors.
- weapons animation are all the same, along with fist spells, wish elements played a role against enemies more.
- combat can be repetitive after you become OP and autotarget can cause issues if you face an npcs you could accidentally hit them sometimes.
- difficulty scaling could have some improvement.t
- Voice is decent, main character sounds like Christian Bale's Batman.
- Graphics needs updated engine, decent at max
- camera can be clunky during dialogue sometimes
- The item interface can be reworked much better, hate having to hotbar everything to use it such as self cast spells, also need rework on keybindings.
-  The game could interact button instead of the attack button as interact, sometimes you accidently just talk to your companion in the fray of things or clicking to find loot because it is all one button.
- Need patch to fix 8 core limitation that is causing a blackscreen
- spells are a lackluster
- World empty after you kill everything, it doesn't respawn so no more mobs respawn.

It's LEGO, it's LotR.  You really can't go wrong.  I've thoroughly enjoyed the game so far, having completed the main story and finshed about half of the extra stuff.  The open world is fun to explore, the main quest line is filled with the typical LEGO humor while staying true to the movies, and the crafting adds a nice twist compared to previous LEGO games i've played.  All in all, i highly recommend the game; it's a blast at any age.
As far as negatives, about the only complaints i have can be summed up in 2 points.  One, i wish the "open world" was more open; there are many areas that look like you should be able to get to that you either hit an invisble wall or "bounced" back to a safe spot - something that always irks me in games.  Second, there are quite a few random bugs to be found.  Getting your character stuck on a shrub or rock, objects that don't break when they are supposed to, and several reported "100% denying" issues where the save doesn't record you completing objectives that you can't complete a second time.  Personally i haven't ran into any of the last, but there are quite a few reports of people who have, so i recomend being cautious when going for a 100% completion.  About the only other negative i can think of is the fact that you can only use 4 save slots, something i find ridiculous for any PC game.  I realize it's a port, but still - there's just no reason to limit the number of saves on essentially any platform nowadays.
Other than that, i've highly enjoyed this faithful-to-the-source game, and recomend it to anyone looking for a casual, fun time!

Reaching almost 500 hours since OBT atm. I think I'm ready to write a review about this game, but most people won't like it.
Overal, I highly suggest this game to everyone! Yes the game is a huge grind even if You are so called p2w player.
There is no such thing as drone/turrets etc. problem, if You learn how to counter them. Most people who complain about this issue are Canon players who can't aim.
Many people also will say that Hover builds have way too much armor, but they don't know what they are talking about. To put it in simple words at 10k+ Power score ground Vehicle easily can have 3000+ structure, where good Hover builds will have only around 1000. But even if people can't counter Hover builds, changes are coming to the parts and fairly soon I guess.
People also are saying that weapons like spears are now useless against hover builds, but they might be surprised how effective they can be if mounted high enough to hit hover builds.
Reading some reviews I also see that people are saying that after 3k+ PS drones and hover builds are ruling the battlefield. ALL of those people are wrong! as I said I have almost 500 hours in the game and 80% I played missions with 3,5k-4k PS and honestly if it's not for a 4man groups Hovers and drones was never a problem to Me personally!
So now to my personal review and why I am making it positive!
1. Ranked battles for competitive players! Yes it will take months to grind before You can participate and get in top 100, but it's possible, I personally only recently started to participate, so I would say that for ok player it will take around 400 in game hours before You can do good in Ranked battles.
2. fast matches - PVP match only lasts 3 minutes, so You have to move around instead of camping! Many people still either camp, either suicide!
3. skill to win! Yes many people think that there are a lot of cheaters in this game, but I don't think so! In my around 400 ranked battles so far, I haven't seen even once aimbot or anything from that sort. Yes there have been some lucky shots that got Me killed, but I haven't noticed visible cheating. It really takes skill and a lot of practice to do good in hover builds, specially combined with Tsunami canons!
4. season missions - I completed every season mission since OBT start, it's a great way to earn a lot of crafting materials together with some containers. It used to be every week, now changed to every 2 weeks, means that You really need to spend only 1 hour a day in order to earn in 2 weeks a lot of scrap, wires, enough electronics and on top of that 1 rare and 1 epic part, which can be sold, meaning that around 400 coins every 2 weeks besides selling earned crafting materials.
5. In game market - Market is an awesome feature that can help You if You use it right. Before a major update selling some of Your stuff will benefit You greatly, after new major update drops, quick buy/sell is a thing and can earn You a lot of coins in short amount of time. My quick example would be right after Dawns children update dropped I had 1300 coins on my account, new pack came out and people sold their Icarus hovers. I used that into my advantage and did a quick buy/sell with these hovers in first 2 days I earned over 2000 coins by just buying and selling these hovers.
6. Brawls - Specificly The big black scorpions brawl, where everyone is equal and it all depends on Your personall skill.
If You haven't tried it, try it and thank Me later.
Overal Awesome game, still needs a lot of work at end game, simply because there are only 3 good building options currently for it. More works, but to do very good it's either Double Tsunami hover builds, Double Hammerfall builds or Tripple Spark builds. Drones etc. works too, but because they are passive builds it often leads into defeats. mandrake builds also work good if people know how to use them right, but then again skilled players normally know how to counter that.
I could go on and on, but simply it takes a lot of time to learn the game, but when You do it's great fun and well worth effort!

Having spent many hours trying dwarf fortress, getting to a level of modest but below average competence, but always finding the interface to much hassle to work with to come back to very often, I've been looking for a good graphical colony simulator for a long time. All I wanted was something easy to navigate, something where each colonist felt interesting and individual (and thus you actually care about them a bit), and where there was plenty to do to build something self maintaining. I've tried a few and nothing really held my attention .. until Rimworld.
It captures so many of the fun parts of dwarf fortress (colonist Bob getting unhappy because the new arrival ex-lover happens to be a sister of another colonist that he was making passes at, which then makes the ex-lover start a fight with the sister who goes crazy, runs off to the wild, starving until she gets shot by a raider who was passing by - this is not a contrived cliche, these stories are commonplace and great). It has research, the ability to make cool stuff out of daft materials that makes no sense which you can then sell to traders with poor taste, it has pets that breed out of control and carry stuff for you. The only thing that dwarf fortress has that I noticeably missed was excellent handling of fluid management, but I can live without that.
Colonists can be pyromaniacs and repeatedly set fire to your crops because they're bored, they can refuse to fight just because they're pacifists, they can lose body parts from entire arms to single toes (which can almost always be replaced by amusing prosthetics), they can be homosexual, they can have drug addictions, there's so much "flavour" to each member of your colony that it's easy to grow attached to specific colonists.
Raiders, heatwaves, toxic clouds of radioactive waste, animals going mad and attacking everyone, there are numerous events to ruin your day that you can tweak (both the frequency and severity) and change on the fly midgame, and there's even the somewhat-beta-ish ability to run more than one colony at a time.
Summary
Not everyone's cup of tea unless you like micromanagement colony games, but if you've always wanted to get into Dwarf Fortress but been put off by the ASCII, this is the closest you'll get, falling short in some areas but surpassing it in others, and capturing the "feel" of the game like nothing else I've played yet.

All in all I love this game, but I have one gripe. Honestly the combat is really lacking, even if it is an improvement. No matter how good you seem to get with the combat, you are nearly guaranteed to get hit a couple times fighting a group of two (or three if you have a companion) and if you are fighting a group of three or up you will not avoid damage. That is just how it is. Combat does not allow you to get good enough to really protect yourelf while you deal damage. I found dodging to be more effective than blocking after a bit but still, it was just impossible to really avoid damage... Which really sucks to me because I liked to play games "perfectly" if you will. No mistakes and such. That doesn't matter in this game.
But anyway, like I said I love this game, it is great, just don't expect to be to awesome in combat. You will be able to deal pretty heavy damage eventually though. 8/10 for me, only combat holds this game back in my eyes.

*NEW REVIEW UP
-New Review after 20+ hours in the game-
I'm going to write this review from a Gothica/Risen fans PoV. You will have to understand PB games to appreciate this game. it is a niche game for players who like hard combat Action RPG's like Dark Souls.
-For returning players from the Gothica/Risen universe, PB made a solid game in Risen 3. The engine is a more efficient less buggy redo of Risen 2, so the graphics and physics are techinaly the same but have now been recoded for less bugs, locked high frame rates, and less stress on your hardware. So if you're looking for a new top of the lin graphics engine on par with a PS4 game don't expect much. The Game was released on 360/ps3/WinPC, so it's made for last gens hardware.
You play a new hero, you are not the nameless figure from Risen 1 and 2, but instead you are one of the sons of Captain Steelbeard, your sister is Patty and you start off the game together.
==FOR NEW PLAYERS==
Pirahna Bytes, aka PB, is known for making EXTREMELY STORY driven RPG's with DIFFICULT COMBAT mechanics. Not combat thats clunky, but combat that reflects starting off as a new character, as you gain skills in combat training you will notice the improvement and growth of your character. If you're new to this kind of game, then the start of the game (first 4 hours) will be a pain in the butt for you. But you will feel your character grow and get a real sense of accomplishment as you gain more skills and stats. It's one of the staples of PB games and it makes it a very niche genre not unlike Dark Souls is a niche genre. I highly suggest purchasing Risen 1 since it's dirt cheap and has no DLC to get a feel for PB games. if this is your first PB game and you don't like the game style you will feel ripped off, but I don't feel ripped off, I love it.
==COMBAT==
Combat will be more in line with Risen 1, then in Risen 2. More emphasis on dodging, and reading opponents ques, understanding when they combo attacks and when what they do when you dodge, moving in combat to avoid getting ganged up on, and choosing when to attack is key. Unlike Risen 2 you will not be able to move from Parry to Attack seamlessly, lending a step of difficulty more in line with traditional PB games. Which for PB fans is great, Risen 2 had hard reviews from PB veterans for making the game more cupcake and less hardcore. So Risen 3 is a step in the right direction.
==CRAFTING==
Unlike Risen 1 and 2, weapon crafting actually has a USE in this game. A new feature is that you take some of the misc items and combine them with weapons to make a better weapon (Thrusting sword + 2 silver plates+6 iron ore) gets you a Disked Epee, with better stats of couse, it is very money effecient. This is also in line with Guns, Muskets, and all melee weapons, even with the unqiue weapons that require difficult to find parts can be upgraded with lots of rare mats to make superior verions or to change it's damage type. Example the Crest Wave SLASHING sword 55-85 Damage +10 Slashing can be changed to the "Lightning" 55-85 Piercing +10 Piercing *and it has electric particle skin and can partialy pierces blocks*
Potion crafting is back along with the rare + perm stat potions made from the perm stat ingredients, The raw ingredients give +2, the potions give +5
More emphasis on temp buff potions is used since there are more skills to allocate your Glory(XP) too. So expect to use buff potions often to surpass early Lockpicks, Persuade, and Pickpocket checks
==GAME LENGTH==
24.5 Hours into the game at the time of this review, i am still in chapter 2, I have 4 islands explored,  2 islands un explored, and just started my 5th island. Like a good book, PB games tend to have 3 acts, I have not chosen one of the 3 factions available yet, and don't expect too until I'm near the end of chapter 2. I have only encountered 2 of the main factions so far. The games factions are the Guardians/Mages from Risen 1, the Voodoo Pirates from Risen 2, and the new faction are the Demon Hunters. You will spend hours revisting islands to find more quests, NPC's, loot, buried treasures, and open hidden passages. These do not feel like tacked on back tracking to add game time thank goodness, but honest progression, both in character development and story. I expect to drop 40-55 hours on the campaign easily.
==OVER ALL IMPRESSION SCORE==
Using 10/10 as a base line for Risen 1
Gothica 3 beng 9/10
and 6/10 as a Baseline for Risen 2
and 4/10 as Gothic 4: Arcania
and 1/10 being Daikatana or Superman 64
I give Risen 3 a 8.5/10
Graphics 7/10
The graphics are last gen but RECENT last gen, so they are smooth FPS on Max graphics and are plenty pretty, PB games aren't known for shiny, they are known for superb story and gameplay.
Combat 9/10
Not as varied or complex as Risen 1, it is much better then Risen 2, you can still feel your character grow, and get that sense of accomplishment. PB vets/fans should play on HARD. Pb did a great job getting back to it's roots.
Story 10/10
Well written and capable of being a book, deep and lengthy but not stale, and a continuation from Risen 1 and 2. It's fantastic, a game with great plot, it is perfect for the Single Player western RPG fans who miss plot.
Is this game worthy of the PB saga? Yes it is, it is a redeeming light for PB since the goofs of Gothica 4 and Risen 2. A great sign that they are getting back in touch with what made them our favorites. I would compare Risen 3 with Deus Ex 3 in terms of taking a step in the proper direction to it's roots.
Is the game worth the 49.99 USD price tag? YES, most new games cost 59.99 USD, some Early Access games cost as much as 125 USD and are utter crap. 10 dollars cheaper the most AAA games and a positive growth in game style for PB fans makes this a steal!
PB vets should buy Risen 3 if you are on the ropes.
NEW PB PLAYERS should buy Risen 1 or Gothica 1,2 or 3 to see if this is the game style you;d enjoy. Feel free to read my review for Risen 1 to see what I mean.

As a DBZ fan, I was going to get this game either way, if it was bad or not. I looked at some reviews online and by the looks of it, this game was BAD. However, a lot of Steam Users say it was a game worth getting, so I purchased the game and was a bit reluctant to see how the game would do. Let me just start out, by saying the $50 was worth it. Sure, like every game, there's flaws and server crashes when a game comes out.
PROS
+Good Customization. 5 Different races to choose from, heights, hair, chins, everything. The customization in this game really lets you explore some of the races of your favorite characters from DBZ. They're all balanced in a way. with different stats for each race and gender you choose.
+Combat. Some might say it's good or bad, but to me, it's a good fighting system. The combos, ki blasts, super attacks, ultimate attacks, evasive skills, transformations, and dodges are all fun to use. You can explore the different attacks and transformations from some of the characters in the DBZ world.
+Co-Op. Having another friend when playing the game can turn out to be rather enjoyable. The Parallel Quests are missions you can do alone or with 1-2 other friends to earn EXP and Loot and Skills. Having a friend alongside me while fighting all the major villains in the game can really make the replay value of the game boost.
+Story. This can be a con or a pro, depending on your background. If you're playing this game as a fan of DBZ, you'll enjoy the story, as I did. However, if you have as to no slightest clue as to who even Raditz or Nappa is, then you won't understand the story much. (if you don't even know much of DBZ, why would you get the game anyway??) The story doesn't explain much of the events you're trying to fix. The basic things you're told consists of Trunks telling you to beat the bad guy and let things flow into place, and if you're a DBZ fan, you know how the events will turn out and go on as they're supposed to. If you don't have any background knowledge on the DBZ story, you'll be left asking, "Why did I do that? How is this supposed to help?" When you end up not being able to save Tien, Yamcha, Piccolo, and Chiatzou, you'll be left wondering, 'How was that a good thing?" when Trunks tells you, that's how things are supposed to happen.
+ Graphics. The graphic style of the game really fits the game perfectly. Not much to say, but other than the graphics are great.
Con
-Connectivity. Sure, I got this game roughly two weeks after it came out, so some of the server issues were ressolved, but not completely. Sometimes, I'll randomly be logged out of my character, becuase of server issues or I lost Server Connection, when I have perfect WiFi connection. Sure, games come out with server problems, but it's still happening to this day. A sign will pop up occasionally when I'm in a battle online, and it says, "Server Connection Lost" and it takes me back all the way to the starting page of the game. Multiplayer battles against someone can sometimes be laggy or resulting in a "Server Connection Lost" and can be frustrating at times.
Overall, this game is a great game. It's mechanics, graphics, co-op, combat, and customizaton really brings out the game in a great way. I have to admit, since I'm a DBZ fan, I was bias torward a good review for the game, but netherless, I didn't have to be a fan to still enjoy the game. The only downfall is the server connection issues, but I'm sure the issues could be ressolved soon enough. Overall, I'd rate the game a 9/10.

Mabinogi... is a thing. It has soo much content that you simply cannot do everything unless you dedicate all your time to playing. You can easily get lost in the game so much that you are planning and checking the Wiki constantly for how to do something.
Graphics - While not the best graphics, the graphics themselves are fairly good. They fit in very well with the game's style. However, the Physical (collision, movement) portion of the graphics are complete crap. This is likely to do with the engine or bad net coding as a result of the poor engine. But the displacement lag among other things make this game something to yearn for.
Content - You are not prepared. I do not know of any game that has the level of content that Mabinogi that is actually useful at all times. Unlike games like WoW, Mabinogi quests stay useful and do not go obsolete. The 'Generations' keep moving forward and new players start right from the begining. None of that "Oh hey, you can do quests... but you will really only get to experience the current xpac and everything else is a faceroll" kind of deal. There is also a very interesting and very long story to be told if you are interested in the RP aspect.
Combat - Combat, as stated in the Graphics, is kind of meh. I think it could Vastly be improved if DevCat/Nexon took the time to upgrade the engine and fix the problems plauging the game. But, that will take time. I just hope it is in the pipeline soon. I actually think the combat style itself is very tactical and interesting, but suffers harshly because of the engine issues and terrible net coding.
The game can be a bit hard on new players and players seeking to do the generations may find themselves struggling. Vetrans think the generations are too easy while new players think they are too hard. The game does have scaling built in, where it gives harder monsters based upon your combat power, but it has not been properly updated in some time.
Overall, I would recommend the game if you like anime MMO's. Mabinogi has something not seen in other games so it is worth trying out (it is free after all). I think Mabinogi could have a very bright future if DevCat/Nexon start focusing on the ever-present problems with the game. But, you do learn to live with them and find quite a bit of joy playing the game. Whether you like to fight with magic, range, or close combat, you like to craft, make stuff, or trade, mabinogi has it.

I would not recommend this or any "cookie-cutter" game maker software to someone who wants to produce a finished commercial product.  When it comes to RPGs these days, you need more than a tremendous story/characters/dialogue or else your product will never get noticed.  When you use "cookie-cutter" game makers, that story aspect is the only originality you can provide.
But within certain contexts, RPG Maker MV is simply amazing.  I want to spend a year designing maps, story, characters and dialogue for my RPG.  Most of the original aspects to my proposed product revolve around audio and combat, which aren't possible with RPG Maker MV.  Hard to tell if your proposed story/character mechanics will work until you play them, and it's hard to motivate to spend a year coding software (for me, AGK2) so I can BEGIN playtesting the story.
No chicken n' egg problem if you have something like RPG Maker MV.  You can develop both simultaneously, because it's so simple to work with RPG Maker MV.
So if you're approaching RPG making like I am, I can't recommend this enough.  I'm only a half hour in and I've already got most of the basics down (to emphasize, I have a coding background which aids with immediately understanding certain structures that RPG Maker MV is essentially a shell for, even though it's not involving direct coding at all).  If you're looking for something that will be the final product, and sell it for money, I'd have to roll my eyes, yes, yes.

Let's give this another shot without the pointless tangent:
This is a Korean MMORPG and everything that might lead you to suspect, by which I mainly mean that sometimes the whole code feels like a house of cards ready to blow up in a storm of bugs and embarassment at seemingly any or no provocation. This is compounded by a proneness to serious lag, which loves to pop up in the middle of combat just to murder your face for trying. Many-to-most features of the game are quite opaque and tricky to understand, and there's a lot of grindy crap.
But, uh... Well, I enjoy it. It gets easier to enjoy as you get used to its flaws, I think.
The combat would actually be quite fun if only it were less laggy and buggy, as it does at least have a nice weight to it. And then, if you'd rather not fight so much, well, there's just so much to friggin' do in this game. Go into one of many schools of combat if you want, or choose a more peaceful lifestyle of commerce or production, bearing in mind that you'll almost certainly want to be able to hold up in a fight whatever you do. It's a big and engaging world that's fun to just hang around in. The playerbase is... hmm. Well, it's... you can find some good folks, but I'm just glad it's easy to blacklist people.
If you end up paying for anything, it will probably be pets, which can serve all kinds of useful functions to include simple combat backup and extra inventory space. You'll want inventory space.
Anyway the point is, this is the sort of game where you can lose yourself for a long time if you're not careful. I seem to get a little more lost every time I come back to it. Honestly I'm okay with it. It's impressively far from perfect, but ultimately a good time.

Hero Siege is a hack and slash rpg from in indie game studio.  This game can be great fun, it helps to have friends to play with like most online games.  It seems that the Devs have a thing for the diablo series, the referances are abound(from Shakos to enigma armors and more) Like any normal RPG you go through levels beating minibosses and a final boss at the end of each act.  Once some one makes a game up to 3 others can join.  Max level is 150 but after that you get extra levels that increase your stats 1 level = 10 to each stat.  The extra levels go across all your max level charicters, so once you get a 150 with (13) extra levels any charicter you get to 150 will get the extra 130 stat boost ***note since update  The xp needed to gain a hlvl has gone up but the stat bonus has gone from 10 to 25.**
Pros -
Many classes to choose from (You get more with DLC)
Fast quick action ingame
Easy to learn
Vast amounts of gear and combos
Tons of Relics you pick up that do veriaty of things (these do go away once you die, but you get them at the end of levels and in shops)
Cons-
Online gameplay can be buggy (game crashing occurs too often)
The community is hit or miss, meet some great people but there are alot of beggers and anoying people.
Dev team is small so it can be a bit to get bugs fixed
The prices is alittle steep since all the DLCs are pricey too
I will point out that the Collectors editions include things like Skins and Eye Candies but the normal DLCs have the Classes and levels.  I was a Huge Diablo 2 nerd and this is a great new game for those that like D2.
Over all I really enjoy the game.  I hope to see it grow.

I found this game to be a waste of $50.  I mean, the game looks and feels like a game i played back in 2003, and it's not even as good as that one.  Now, let me elaborate a bit on what i found to be bad about different parts of the game.
First and foremost, the combat system. Absolutely awful combat; it feels like you're playing an RTS game(They attack, you block, you attack, they block or don't).  Not to mention the fact that it's nearly impossible to kill more than one enemy if you don't have a follower.  To sum this one up, the combat is, like i said earlier, an annoying RTS game.
Next let's talk about the voice acting.  It's horrendous.  I mean, the way people talk makes it impossible for you to be immersed.  To sum this one up, you'd be better off using JUST the subtitles.
And last, let's talk about the graphics.  Well, there isn't much to say about the graphics, seeing as they are pretty non-existent(that's an exaggeration, of course). But really, they are pretty awful-even on max to near max settings.
To sum this one up, the graphics are similar to that of a game made back in around 2010(Just an estimate)
Now, to sum everything up, i would avoid this game unless you are a hardcore Risen fan that doesn't mind poor game development, or you just don't mind poor game development and think this game is fun.

Rosebud Condominium may seem like yet another casual video game, but hidden behind this facade hides a critical videogame that imparts an important life lesson. The heroine, Sarah, is indeed aspiring to stratospheric heights. Joining her are two mysterious men; her "boss" who has mandated to her the impossible task of creating the tallest condominium that the world has yet to see, and Craig, whose various schemes are a constant threat to the completion of her out of this world project. Rosebud Condominium is a masterpiece in that it is able to present the concept of futility under the guise of a lighthearted video game. But of course, only the most intelligent can see through this facade. As such, it is able to provide both a meaningful life message and a worthwhile amount of gameplay. If you have the time and money to play a video game, then I suggest that you get Rosebud Condominium to experience how a seemingly mundane video game can serve as a medium to impart important life lessons.

***Updated*** I was asked to be less vague about the combat issues.
Maybe worth $20-$30, graphics and animations are sub par. Not terrible, but nothing special to look at even on max settings.
Combat is clunky and boring, I'm one for diffuiculty, but this is just frustrating.
The game is unclear to areas you should be going too. Dailogue is so bad an uninteresting, they try to spice it up with curse words.
It's not about them holding my hand, I went to the begining island after the intro chapter. I fooled around with getting some new gear at the shop and upgrading some skills. Even with these upgrades I would be 2-3 shot by an enemy.
You get a light attack, a medium attack, a cheap shot (your pistol), a parry and a dodge.
Light attack- everything is faster than you, the chance of attacking and not getting hit at least a few times is slim. Wouldn't be a problem if I didn't die in a couple of hits.
(Yes there are potions, but excessive prices and the amount of damage you take eats up your money fairly quickly)
Heavy attack- needs to charge and is slow, 75% of the time the monster just jumps away from you and you miss.
Cheap Shot- This is kind of cool, but damage is weak and you only have a finite amount of ammo or throwing knifes.
Parry- this is useless most of the time, even an enemies light attack can break your guard and since most enemies double attack you get hit anyway. A parry is supposed to break the momentum of enemies opening them for an attack. This is a crappy block function at best.
Dodge- My least favorite mechanic, your recovery time almost always leads to you getting hit by a follow up attack or another enemy.
You end up just blocking and dodging waiting for your companion to kill things. I don't need to be the god of war, but I don't appreciate being a punching bag either.
The real draw back to the dialogue is the horrible animations, making it almost unbearable to sit through even a 30 second engagement.
I'm sure the game gets better, but almost 2 hours in and I can't even stand to look at it anymore. Reminds me of two worlds, if you remember what that was like I would steer clear of this title.
In short I would not recomend buying this until it goes on sale and only if you are an older style rpg fan, or you really enjoy the series.

In short:
What you won't found here is pretty graphics or voice acting or deep story. Also it does have steep learning curve and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI for the civilians that will run into the zombies in an attempt to run from them(WTF). For some reason they run to their death faster than they run to their rescue.
On the plus side: it's a sorta-roguelike, real time tactics (with planning phase just before the onslaught begins) funny game with minimalistic graphics about surviving a zombie infestation. Also HIGHLY MODDABLE which is great.
The intersting mechanics: each side has it own milestones to achieve and the first side to reach the goal points wins. Some encounters are more defensive (rescue and not really returning fire) and some are all about destroying the other side. It depends on the resources at hand (mostly available mercs), the encounter modifier, the current situation and of course on the player itself.
Can't say I'd recommend it to everyone but for 3$ (when on sale) is at least worth checking out. If the trailer for the game doesn't scare you and you like moddable roguelikes (= high replayability) it is well worth the 10$.

I love the Dragon Ball Universe, the movies (except Bio-Broly), the stories, the characters. I really enjoyed the Budokai and Budokai Tenkaiichi Series. Also, I am a fan of the RPGs. I like the concept of leveling up and developing new strategies. This game is a very solid first try, but it ultimately is a disappointment to me.
I love the idea of creating your own character, even though it is a little limited. My own created Saiyan is a dream I have had once before. The worst part of having your own created Saiyan in my opinion is how the Kaioken and Super Saiyan 1 & 2 works. It is very similar to DBZ Budokai 1, where your transformation heavily burn ki (stamina for kaioken). I was hoping you would just stay Transformed, but not in this game. For your created character, Super Saiyan can earned through loot drops (RPG element) or you can buy it at the store. That is really disappointing too. Which level Super Saiyan does not matter, just your level.
The mission design is a mixed bag. Some are fun, but the collect all the dragon ball sucks. The main missions often require you to grind in the parallel mission to reach the proper level to even compete properly. Perfect example, after the android saga, I was only 31 after a bit of parallel mission grinding. The very next main mission was a fight with a level 42 Mira. When my character attacked him, he was remained stoic and killed me in 1-2 minutes, so I had to spend a few hours grinding up to about level 38 before I could fight him. Worst level spike ever. Earlier I got stuck in a main mission fighting Frieza's henchmen and I kept failing the mission, because 1 of my partner character dying. I annoying mission failure clauses are awful.
The in-game dialogue is not good. The lines are delievered almost as bad as the original Resident Evil 1. The in-game cutscene dialogue breaks throwing of the timing very often, causing the NPC to start his/her next sentence before they have finished the previous sentence.
Though it is a PC title, this game does not support a high resolution monitor. My laptop's resolution is 3840 x 2160, but that resolution totally breaks the aura and ki effects. To use these effects, you must turn your monitor down to 1920 x 1080, or these effects will not work. The game does run at 60 FPS cap on my laptop, which is good. However, the game crashes every time I try to open the graphics options. I have no idea what the graphic option look like, because the game crashes EVERY SINGLE TIME! It really is just faster to crash the game, then properly log out.
The hub world, where all the other online players gather, is so disappointing. My first problem with this hub world is that it is a No-Fly Zone. I can't believe there is no flying here, just a totally useless jump button. You can't jump on anything in this game. You just run around everywhere, slowly. Every one of the 4 part hub world areas require a loading screen. And there is just a large space of nothing to do. A little PVP here would have been good.
The supposedly open world flying is much smaller than I had hoped with invisible walls everywhere. The scenery is much less destructible than the Budokai Tenkaiichi series. You can fly to any areas freely, you have to go through an annoying little portal. The energy beam attacks travel very short distances and when 2 energy beams collide, they just cancel. No energy beam duels in this game. They have just thrown it out in this game.
This game feels like a good start to a great MMO-ish DBZ Universe experience, but there are just too many bugs, missed opportunies, and progression issues. My friends have already bought and resold this game to over people on console and I really understand the disappointment. I really had high hopes. I still have high hopes for DB Xenoverse 2, or perhaps an expansion that fixes these issues. I really want to love this game, but I really just can't.

TL;DR too much walking, not enough enemies, not enough guns, bad aiming
There are many flaws in Borderlands which stop it from being a really good game. I mean, a really fun and good game. It feels like a good concept for a game built on a pillar of call of duty gameplay; the game is a bad hybrid of modern shooter "gameplay" (if you can even call it that) and actually fun oldschool arcade gameplay. Quite simply, you can tell that there is not much talent behind the creaters behind this. They just got lucky and made a somewhat fun game.
The level design of this game is quite bad. The game is very slow in its introduction to start becoming fun. You do not have your ability until level 5, and the guns are very much basic ones. The dungeons are all more or less the same. At least they had the decency in many dungeons, to design shortcuts from the end of the dungeon to the beginning. Then there's walking. there is walking and walking from point A to B (and no, this "sprinting" is no sprint. Call me back when the character is as fast as doomguy). This is okay on maps where there are vehicles; on maps without them, it's a huge pain. Honestly I have spent more time in this game walking from point A to B then fighting. The setting is made by many levels and semi-hubs. You go to one town, which has 3 dungeons or enemy areas on the outskirts of its map. You do typical chores, or I'm sorry, "missions" like killing 10 chickens in this that dungeon and collecting this that artifacts of an ancient civilization 1000 years ago (original story, do not steal). Sounds familiar, right? Now, borderlands makes this fun by having crazy loads of weapons and crazy loads of enemies. Or so it tries.
There is no 67 bajillion guns. There's several models for the base, handle, scope, and other accessories for each type of gun, and different colors for each model. These parts are randomly placed together, with randomly generated stats. Now this is totally fine if there were many models for each of the above. But there isn't, that's the thing. After a while, you notice the trends in the gun models and notice that you get the same gun over and over, just with slightly different numbers. Also, the difference in the guns are somewhat superficial. There are guns which reload faster, zoom more, fire faster, have more accuracy, and have more ammunition per magazine. Pretty boring right? But then, there's possible elemental effects for each type of gun, possibility of the gun acting like other types of guns (shotguns which fire rockets, revolvers with shells etc). It leads into something that could be exciting, but then it stops there. The are only so many REALLY crazy guns, like the TK's wave shotgun where the bullets bounce from the ground... and I can't remember any more. There isn't♥♥♥♥♥♥like in painkiller where you shoot lightning and shurikens. Hell, there isn't even miniguns in this game! It's like as if this game was designed by people who only ever played call of duty and Wowt. What about sniper rifles which shoot tornadoes with swords slashing inside them? What about shotguns which shoot slimes onto enemies which can poison others? Why aren't there rocket launchers which shoot moais that get bigger as they get damage until they finally explode?
As you would imagine, the amazing 67 gajillion guns play worse than call of duty. Rubbish hip fire and iron sights. The only valid guns from a distance, if you want critical hits, are those with 95+ accuracy. There's also this really annoying thing where you lose your aim when you get shot, so you cant pick off headshots with a sniper rifle or revolver because every time you try doing so, the aim in iron sights randomly goes upwards. Not to mention, the bullet lag is ridiculous. It doesn't help that the AI is complete garbage and ALWAYS knows where you are, so there's no flanking (unless you use your special ability, but that's less fun). The only valid weapons are high-repeating ones, but maybe this is because I played as soldier. Also, gainig experience in guns can ruin the game if you get too much experience in one gun, because every other gun type starts to feel pointless. If you get an accurate assault rifle, with assault rifle perks and skills, that's it. You main that gun forever. Did I also mention that the guns sound and feel like they are plastic?
There is not much enemy variety at all. There are people, which range from psychos, midgets, normal ones, and armored ones. Each have interesting ways in which they fight against you. Psychos are melee only so you can prioritize killing them later, which is thrilling because you have to judge when you have to kill this axe wielding madman, who is right in front of you, compared to the man in the distance who is shooting you. Midgest are mostly comic relief, but you need to be careful because they can escape your line of sight. The armored ones require you to aim outside of their shield, or may even require headshots (if I recall). The headshot for skags is when they open their mouths, while for those bug things it's their jelly backs. There isn't much way of defending against enemy attacks, however. It's a matter on how fast you can kill them with how much you can aim for their heads. Also, there aren't that many enemies at once. It would be really fun if the game played like serious sam where there are a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of enemies and you have to move in order to attack them. You are too slow to dodge anything in Borderlands. You can't hide behind cover because the enemies always know where you are. So you simply go backwards, distancing youself from the enemy, and you try to kill the enemy first. The few enemies are fairly fun to play against. But you will kill, thousands upon thousands of the same guys over and over again, to the point where it's boring.
On another note, I have to say that you will laugh your♥♥♥♥♥off at midgets. Also, the second wind mechanic is great. By keeping a low health enemy near you as you nearly die, you can essentially never die in this game. It's some fun, basic strategy.
I can't comment on the balance of the characters, but Berserker has a really boring ability. Soldier's turret is alright. It's kind of superficial though. I guess you are supposed to pick characters on what kind of gameplay you like, but you are stuck with that for that entire game. You can't switch classes for the same build.
The DLC's mess up the balance of the game, because it was made so that you start playthrough 2 of the original game straight after playthrough 1. But if you play through the DLC's playthrough 1, you start playthrough 2 being too powerful, killing the pace of the game.
The optimization is terrible. I get FPS slowdowns when there are many objects in the viewing distance, on my computer which has an i7 and a GTX 760.
The music is very minimal. The music by elephant in the cage, in the beginning, is the highlight of the musical composition in this game.
No comment on the graphics.
The game is mighty fun when you are blowing up loads and loads of enemies in the face with a superfast submachine gun or shotgun that has flammable bullets, and just mowing those bullet sponges down. No really, it's actually damn fun, even when you are alone. It's even more fun with friends (then again everything is more fun with friends). There's just a lot of walking inbetween, with no ability to aim accurately from a distance. I want to blast things close up in the face while at the same time picking off headshots with my sniper rifle from hip fire.
I can only recommend this game to you if you like loot, guns, comic art, and RPG's like I do. Otherwise, stay away form this game.

There are few games which truly captures the essence of survival. All to often, a game forces you to follow a closed narrative of a protagonist or group. However, unlike many modern titles, Rimworld have succeeded in creating an immersive open world experience which in my opinion few can match.
Rimworld is an open world survival reminiscent of minecraft (sort of) where you build you base, collect resources and defend against those who wish to raid and pillage. Take control over your individual colonists, assign them work and watch them day by day slave away at collecting resources. As your colony grows in size, chains of production grows more complex and the items you produce more advanced. From mere pistols to building futuristic charge rifles, Rimworld challenges you to build an colony which will stand the test of time. Do you have the food to sustain winter? What can you improve to expand supply of iron? How will you defend against an horde of raiders, both better equipped and growing in numbers?
Even though vanilla version is filled to the brim with content, Rimworld's vibrant modding community is where the heart of the game lies. With full Steam workshop support (thanks to a amazingly flexible developer). Mods adds those few extra quirks which adds hundreds of hours of gameplay aswell as practical tools to improve the mechanics of the game. Want to build a nuclear reactor? Just download the expanded enrgy production mods. Your colony grown too big to micromanage? Subscribe to the colony manager mod. I hate survival games. I have several and I've tried them out with varying levels of success, but they've never managed to hold my interest. So what is it about RimWorld that has its claws in me? Or because you can be as good or evil as you want in the game and your actions actually do matter. Kill a group that came to check you out? Prepare to be raided by that faction. Kill off an unwanted colonist? The rest are might upset and may or may not decide this is the last straw and - oh, I don't know - start a murderous killing spree or just wander aimlessly until they collapse from hunger and exhaustion.
The label says this is an early access game, but don't believe it. I've had 0 crashes, no reportable bugs, and the modding community is already blossoming and active. In short, this is an amazing game and well worth the cost.

But ignoring the facts of life is no way for me to act...life goes on. So I go on with my life, but I keep my pets within a defineable boundary...close to our home. You can name them. You can customise their body, hair, clothing, skills and personality. You will find that some may be addicted to booze or drugs...they may have a wierd phobia or an old gunshot wound. They eventually want a girlfriend or boyfriend or want to get married. Some have emotional problems or just plain can't stand a particular person. Some are doctors or are spookily good with guns. The Steam Workshop has an almost infinite number of custom content, providing for literally years of replay value. I would recommend Rimworld to my friends and family.        9.8/10
